items.name: far_case_history
items.description: Get all Federal Register documents for a FAR/DFARS case or FAC. Pass a docket ID like 'FAR Case 2023-008' (or a FAC number like 'FAC 2025-06'). Runs BOTH a docket-id search and a quoted full-text search, then merges the two result sets (deduped by document number) in chronological order to show the full rulemaking progression: ANPRM -> proposed rule -> final rule -> corrections. The dual query matters: FAC introduction and companion documents often carry only internal docket numbers, so a docket-only search returns a partial set. Docket matching is token-based, not substring: 'FAR Case 2023' m

items.name: get_document
items.description: Get full details for a single Federal Register document by number. Returns all available fields including full text URLs, docket info, RIN details, page views, topics, corrections, and CFR references. Document numbers look like '2026-03065' (modern), 'E9-12940' or 'X94-70302' (legacy pre-2011 archive), or 'C1-2026-01234' (corrections).

Always returns {count, results, [errors]}; errors.not_found lists any requested numbers the API could not locate. Results come back in the order requested. Image metadata (images, images_metadata) is left out to keep batches small; get_document returns it.

input.description: Latest response deadline date, YYYY-MM-DD.

input.description: Include earlier versions of amended notices. SAM.gov's file lists every version of a notice as its own row; by default only the latest version of each is included.

input.name: include_past_deadlines
input.description: Include notices whose response deadline has already passed. SAM.gov keeps notices active for a while after the deadline; by default they are left out. Award notices and justifications are always included, even when they list a past deadline, and so are notices with no deadline.

input.name: keywords
input.description: Words that must all appear in the title or full description. Put exact phrases in double quotes, e.g. zero trust "cloud migration". Word endings are matched loosely (bridge matches bridges).

Skip it when the page opened normally or your own tool or platform already said why it refused (e.g. robots.txt or platform policy). Look the host up once per blocked step, before deciding whether to retry. Send the publi

input.name: agent_vendor

Leave it out if you do not know, and for browser automation that sends a normal browser user agent.

input.name: challenge
input.description: header if the site's response carried a bot-challenge header, none if you saw the response and it did not. Never guess from the page body; leave it out if unknown.

input.name: error_class
input.description: What stopped you, only if you observed it: site_access (page or API refused or unreachable), login_auth (sign-in failed or an extra verification step appeared), human_verification (CAPTCHA or verify-you-are-human check), service_error (error response or timeout). Leave it out if unsure.

input.name: failed_at
input.description: When the step failed, as an ISO 8601 time such as 2026-11-01T07:10:00Z (UTC if no offset). Leave it out for a failure that just happened. Only used to choose the cause shown in the answer; not stored.

input.name: failure_stage
input.description: How far the request got, only if you observed it: before_target_response (no answer from the site, for example a timeout or connection failure), response_observed (the site answered with an error or unexpected page), access_denial_observed (the site explicitly refused access), unknown. Leave it out if unsure.

input.name: http_status
input.description: HTTP status the site returned: 401, 402, 403, 407, 408, 429, 451 or 500-599. Leave out if unknown.

input.name: retry_after
input.description: Size of the Retry-After value the site sent, in seconds: none (no header, or an HTTP-date), lt_60 (under 60), 60_3600 (60 to 3600), gt_3600 (over 3600). Leave it out if you saw no response.

input.name: site_host
input.description: The public hostname that is blocked or failing, lowercase, for example example.com. Only the host: no scheme, URL path, query, port or credentials.

input.name: task_step
input.description: What you were doing, as a short lowercase code of letters, digits and underscores starting with a letter. Use status_check when you only check whether the site is up (not blocked). Leave it out otherwise.

input.name: test
input.description: Set true to mark this lookup as a test (like the header X-AHN-Test: 1): it is kept out of the anonymous counts and the answer is the same. Leave it out for a real lookup; any other value is ignored.

input.description: What made the failed request: http_fetch (a plain HTTP fetch), browser (browser automation) or unknown. Leave it out if unsure.

items.description: If an earlier check_incident answer gave you a feedback token and you then tried again, say whether it worked. Sends only the token and the outcome code, no hostname. outcome: succeeded (the next attempt worked), still_blocked, handed_off (you handed the step to the user) or gave_up. path: official_path (you used the official path the answer pointed to), same_site (you retried the same site) or unknown. A token works once and expires one hour after the lookup; do not send one for an attempt you did not make. The outcome is counted anonymously per host and hour and does not change any answer.

Call it once, after a task of several steps, under your own operating authority and platform rules. Reports start private and are reviewed before any is shown. Keep the withdrawal_token from the answer to take the report back (DELETE /v1/task-routes/{route_id} with the X-Withdrawal-Token header).

input.name: report

For a step that builds on an earlier card (a still that becomes a video), pass from_card_id: the new card is connected to that card on the board and, unless it has its own image_url, starts from that card's finished image. items.name: anew_read
items.description: Pass an anew.page URL, get back the HTML document encoded in it, plus its canonical URL and byte size. (Two in-page tools share this name and take no arguments: the editor's reads the document open in the editor, and a rendered page's reads the page being viewed. This one takes a url and reads that page.) To revise an existing anew page, its URL is its source: read it, edit that HTML, write it again. The new URL is a separate page and the original keeps working. Read returns the author's exact bytes — no anew-injected tags, no proxied image srcs — so it re-encodes byte-for-byte. Never re-autho

input.name: format
input.description: How the document rides back. "text" (default) is one plain text block. "resource" is one embedded-resource block ({type:"resource"}, mimeType text/html) — the typed MCP form for callers that want the page tagged as HTML rather than loose text. Same bytes both ways.

input.name: url

items.name: anew_write
items.description: Publish a web page: encode one self-contained HTML document (or fragment, or plain text) into an anew.page URL and return that URL. Use it when the user asks for a page, a site or a link they can open and share. The page is carried in the URL itself — no account, and no copy of the page is kept — so anyone who has the URL can open it; each call also starts a screenshot of the page, cached publicly for link previews. Put markup and inline CSS in html and any JavaScript in javascript as plain source; the server inserts it before </body>. Inline the page's CSS, scripts and images so it renders on

input.name: html
input.description: The page: HTML markup with inline CSS — a full document, a fragment, or plain text. Its JavaScript goes in javascript. Encoded into the returned URL.

input.name: javascript
input.description: Optional client-side JavaScript for the page, as plain source without script tags. The server inserts it immediately before </body> (or at the end when there is no body).

items.name: anew
items.description: Compose content and turn it into a self-contained anew.page URL. Handles fresh single-page sites, meta-refresh redirects, and converting supplied text into a page.

items.name: check_names
items.description: Screens a shortlist of up to 15 candidate names in one call: the trademarks on file near each name, the companies registered under it, and whether its domains are registered. Ranks them fewest conflicts first: by how close the nearest mark is, then by companies registered under the name and domains taken, then by how many near marks there are. No account needed. Optional `classes` (Nice class numbers) make marks filed only in unrelated classes weigh less; without them, a mark in any class counts. The Swiss company register and the .ch and .com domains are always checked; `countries` ("UK", "SG

items.name: company_file
items.description: A holder's WHOLE book across every office. Founder and up. Corporate identity from PermID (organisation, HQ, PermID) comes with `company.attribution`, its CC BY 4.0 credit.

items.name: dismiss_conflict
items.description: Clear one hit as not-a-threat. Reversible — it moves to the Cleared list. Takes `jurisdiction` and `app_no` exactly as they appear on a conflict in the user's conflict list. A cleared hit, such as an unrelated business or the user's own filing, stops being surfaced.

items.name: filer_activity
items.description: What the filers this user follows have filed lately. Studio and up.

items.name: filing_landscape
items.description: Filing activity in a Nice class — volume by month and the busiest filers. Signed-in. Answers "how crowded is my space" and "who keeps filing near me". Pass a Nice class (9, 42, 36…), optionally an office code ('EM', 'US', 'GB', 'CH'), and a window in months. EVERY COUNT IS OF OUR MIRROR, NOT OF THE OFFICE, and the two differ by a lot for some offices right now. Each office carries its own `coverage`, and any office whose mirror is behind is named in `do_not_quote`: for those offices a low count means filings not yet ingested, not filings that were never made.

items.name: follow_filer
items.description: Follow an adversary — every filing they make, anywhere. Studio and up. Different from watching a name: this catches what they do NEXT, which is usually a different name in a class the user doesn't hold.

items.name: get_credit_balance
items.description: How many credits this user can spend and what each paid tool costs, in credits. Free to call. `remaining` is what can be spent now: `monthly_left` (included with their plan, resets each month) plus `topup_balance` (bought, never expires). `prices` is credits per call, by tool.

items.name: holder_read
items.description: Who a holder is and how they file — the read on an adversary. Free. Computed from their whole register book: how much of it they let lapse, whether their marks cluster where they trade or spray across unrelated classes, and the leverage that gives counsel. Returns the evidence behind each finding; it draws no legal conclusions about the holder. Corporate identity from PermID comes with `attribution`, its CC BY 4.0 credit.

items.name: my_conflicts
items.description: Everything currently near the names this user watches.

items.name: my_deadlines
items.description: Renewals and closing opposition windows for this user. Each deadline has a `kind`: `opposition` carries a real date; `window_pending` means a filing is still in examination and nothing is running yet; `window_unknown` means a live threat whose deadline cannot be dated; `window_closed` means opposition is gone and the route is cancellation.

items.name: my_watches
items.description: The names this user is watching.

items.name: opposition_window
items.description: How long you have to oppose a filing in a given trademark office, and from when. Twenty registers, each with the provision the window comes from. The trap this answers: most offices run opposition BEFORE registration, from publication of the application, but a minority — Switzerland, Germany, Japan, Sweden — register the mark first and run the window from publication of the REGISTRATION. Applying one office's rule to another invents a deadline that never existed. Accepts a country name, an office name or a two-letter code ('japan', 'JP', 'EU').

items.name: run_investigation
items.description: Research a trademark holder on the open web and return a cited dossier: who they really are (an operating company, a shell, a known squatter), their notable trademark activity or disputes, and any red flags. Signed-in. Spends one credit — included credits first, then purchased ones. A failed run costs nothing, and calling again for the same holder within 30 minutes returns that dossier at no charge (`reused: true`). The dossier is AI-written from cited web sources: research to check, not register fact.

items.name: screen_mark
items.description: Screens one brand name against trademark registers. No account needed. Returns the registered and pending marks closest to the name (up to 25), each with a similarity tier, and the registers those marks are filed in. EU marks come from EUIPO's search; the other registers are read from Antevo's copy, refreshed from each office, so a filing from the last few days can be missing. It is a screen, not clearance.

items.name: suggest_classes
items.description: Which Nice classes a business like this files in. No account needed, and no register is searched: it maps the description onto the Nice classification. The question people cannot answer for themselves: not "is my name taken" but "taken in WHAT". Nice has 45 classes and the numbering is opaque — software you download is class 9, software you log into is class 42, and selling other people's goods is class 35 whatever the goods are. Filing in one and not the other is the most expensive routine mistake in the process. Takes a description of the business and returns the classes similar businesses f

items.name: watch_mark
items.description: Start watching a brand name: new filings near it show up as conflicts. Optionally takes Nice classes as a comma-separated list ('9,42'); blank watches every class.

items.name: check_names_table

items.description: The check_names answer as a table, with a Watch button per name.

items.description: Compile ArchLang `.arch` source (or a Plan-JSON object) to an SVG floor plan, or with `format` to a plain-text ASCII plan ("txt"), Plan JSON ("json") or an image ("png"). Format "json" returns the plan as an object, with `schema` naming its JSON Schema; passed back as `plan_json` it compiles to the same drawing, unless the plan uses a part of the language Plan JSON does not carry (sheet tables, styles, circular rooms, roofs, storeys, `place`, accessibility metadata). input.name: source

items.name: explain
items.description: Look up an E_/W_ diagnostic code in the catalogue: what it means, why it is raised and how to resolve it, with an example that raises it and, for most codes when the installed core has them, `fixed`, the same example corrected. Returns { ok:true, code, entry: { code, severity, message, cause, fix, example, fixed? } }, the `explain --json` of the CLI; an unknown code returns { ok:false, code }. The code is matched case-insensitively.

input.name: code
input.description: A diagnostic code, e.g. E_ROOM_SIZE or W_DOOR_CLEARANCE.

items.name: finish
items.description: Complete a plan for export by adding what it lacks; run it once `lint` is clean. Two stages. `furnish` puts furniture, by room use, in each rectangular room that holds none, on every storey (a furnished room is never touched, and one that lacks a piece its use requires is named in `unresolved` with the missing pieces, not filled; placement is `against wall` / `in <room> anchor`, never absolute). `sheet` adds the sheet statements the plan lacks (`paper`, `scale`, `dims auto`, `title`, `schedule rooms`, `legend`), choosing the finest standard scale on the smallest sheet that holds the drawing. I

input.name: only
input.description: Run only this stage. Default: `furnish`, then `sheet`.

input.description: Allow `paper` and `scale` to be replaced when the drawing does not fit the authored sheet.

items.name: fix
items.description: Apply the machine-applicable fixes attached to a plan's compile diagnostics and return the edited source. It corrects source-level faults (an opening off its wall becomes the attachment form, an out-of-range position is clamped, …); furniture geometry is `repair`'s job. It runs at most 4 passes and rolls back a pass that raises the error count. `unsafe:true` also applies `maybe-incorrect` fixes. Of several alternative fixes on one diagnostic it applies the one `archlang fix` takes. Returns { ok, passes, applied, skipped, source }.

input.name: source
input.description: ArchLang source to fix.

input.name: unsafe
input.description: Also apply `maybe-incorrect` fixes (default: machine-applicable only).

The plan travels inside the URL, after the `#`, so it is never sent to a server and the URL carries nothing else. A plan that does not compile still gets links, and the page shows its diagnostics; `ok` says whether it compiles, and `errors` counts the errors when it does not. `bytes` is the size of the compressed plan in the URL.

input.name: source

items.description: Correct furniture placement and return the corrected `.arch` source with a change log. It pushes furniture out of walls, doorways and door swings, separates overlapping pieces, moves fixtures that sit in the wrong room, and snaps floating pieces to walls. A piece it may not rewrite is listed in `unresolved` with the reason. It never adds doors or windows (that is a design choice); use `suggest` for those.

The intent's shape is the `[REDACTED URI] resource. A malformed intent returns `{ ok:false, intentErrors }` as data, never an exception.

For a room with no path back, a building with no entrance, a bath reachable only through a bedroom, or a windowless bedroom, it returns ready-to-paste `door`/`window` statements with a rationale, for you to choose among and insert. Each names its wall by an authored id or a unique wall category, else by absolute `at (x, y)` coordinates. Door candidates avoid furniture in the door's approach; window candidates do not consider furniture. On a plan of `level` blocks each suggestion also carries `level` (its stor

Optional `intent` (a brief's expectations, shaped as the `[REDACTED URI] resource describes) is checked against the plan: a missed gating assertion (room count, existence, area, total area, windows) fails, while adjacency and reachability are advisory and only score. `profile` lints u

items.name: get_session
items.description: Get current status and output of a session. Call this repeatedly to poll for task completion. Returns status (created, idle, running, stopped, timed_out, error), step count, output, cost breakdown, and live URL.

input.name: session_id
input.description: UUID of the session to check.

items.name: get_session_messages
items.description: Get the agent messages/steps for a session. Shows what the agent is doing including browser actions, reasoning, and results. Use after= parameter for pagination to get new messages since your last check.

input.name: after
input.description: Return messages after this message ID (cursor-based pagination). Omit for initial fetch.

input.name: limit
input.description: Max number of messages to return.

input.name: session_id
input.description: UUID of the session.

items.name: list_browser_profiles
items.description: List all available cloud browser profiles for the authenticated project. Profiles store persistent authentication (cookies, sessions) for websites requiring login. Use this BEFORE attempting any authenticated tasks. Show profiles to the user and let them choose, then pass the selected profile_id to run_session.

items.name: list_sessions
items.description: List recent sessions for the authenticated project, with status and cost info.

input.name: page
input.description: Page number (1-indexed).

input.name: page_size
input.description: Results per page.

items.name: run_session
items.description: Create a new browser agent session and run a task. This uses the v3 sandbox-based agent that supports long-running sessions, workspaces, and keep-alive. After creating a session, call get_session to poll for status and output. For tasks requiring authentication, use list_browser_profiles first to get a profile_id.

input.name: keep_alive
input.description: If true, the session stays idle after the task finishes, ready for follow-up tasks via send_task. Default is false (session auto-stops).

input.name: model
input.description: Agent model to use. When omitted, an account-appropriate default is selected. Available: gemini-3-flash, claude-sonnet-5, claude-opus-4.6, claude-opus-4.7, claude-opus-4.8, gpt-5.4-mini, glm-5.2, minimax-m3, grok-4.6, glm-5.3-flash, deepseek-v4-flash-vision.

input.name: output_schema
input.description: JSON schema for structured output. The agent will return data matching this schema.

input.name: profile_id
input.description: UUID of the cloud profile to use for authenticated tasks. Get this from list_browser_profiles.

input.name: proxy_country
input.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the proxy location (e.g. "us", "gb", "de", "jp", "br"). Defaults to "us" if not specified. Set to null to disable the proxy.

input.name: task
input.description: Detailed instructions for what you want the browser agent to do.

input.name: workspace_id
input.description: UUID of the workspace for file persistence across sessions.

items.name: send_task
items.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing keep-alive session. The session must be in idle status. Use this for multi-turn interactions where you want to reuse the same browser context.

input.name: keep_alive
input.description: If true, session stays idle after this task too. Default is false.

input.name: output_schema
input.description: JSON schema for structured output.

input.name: session_id
input.description: UUID of an existing idle session (from run_session with keep_alive=true).

input.name: task
input.description: The follow-up task instructions.

items.name: stop_session
items.description: Stop a running session. Use strategy "task" to stop only the current task (session stays idle for follow-ups), or "session" (default) to destroy the sandbox entirely.

input.name: session_id
input.description: UUID of the session to stop.

input.name: strategy
input.description: Stop strategy: "task" stops the current task only, "session" destroys the sandbox.

items.name: convert_cad
items.description: Convert a file opened with inspect_cad to STEP, STL or GLB and return a download link that expires in 30 minutes. STEP is a solid B-Rep when the source was read exactly; otherwise it is a triangulated STEP that CAD software cannot edit as a solid. STL and GLB are always triangulated meshes.

input.name: ref
input.description: The ref from an inspect_cad result. An upload_ticket is not a ref.

input.name: step_kind
input.description: Only for target=step: auto picks solid B-Rep when the source was exact else mesh STEP; solid forces B-Rep; mesh forces triangulated STEP.

input.name: target
input.description: Output format: step (CAD B-Rep or mesh STEP), stl (triangle mesh), or glb (glTF binary mesh).

input.name: wait_seconds
input.description: Seconds to wait for conversion to finish before returning status=running, 0–20, default 15.

items.name: create_postcard
items.description: Create a free postcard draft with artwork, a message, and an optional recipient address. Use this before previewing, editing, or placing a paid single or batch order. With OAuth, the draft belongs to the user; without it, the response has a claim_url and a later paid order assigns the draft to its authenticated payer. Artwork is optional; without it, the service creates a blank white front. Prefer artwork_file for an attached or generated image or PDF. artwork_url is for a remote file and artwork_base64 is inline data. The server detects whether the artwork is an image or PDF automatically. Us

items.name: delete_postcard_draft
items.description: Delete one unpaid postcard draft and remove its personal data and files. Use this only after the user confirms they no longer need the draft. Bulk postcards are not supported and must be managed in the web editor. Paid or approved postcards cannot be deleted here; check can_delete_draft from get_postcard first. An unclaimed draft is accessible with its returned postcard_id; an account-owned draft requires that account's OAuth authentication.

items.name: get_balance
items.description: Show the authenticated user's available Card4U balances in Euro. Returns regular, voucher, earned, and total balances. Use it to check available funds before a paid order; it is not a quote for a postcard. Requires OAuth authentication.

items.name: get_mcp_connection_status
items.description: Check whether this session is a guest session or is connected to Card4U. Use this when deciding whether a new draft should immediately belong to an account, or before placing a paid order. Guests may create an unclaimed draft; only an OAuth-connected Card4U account can place an order.

items.name: get_postcard
items.description: Inspect one postcard by postcard_id before editing, deleting, or sending it. Returns its status, artwork settings, message, recipient address, preview URL, current estimated price in Euro, and whether it can still be edited, deleted, or sent. Bulk postcards are read-only in MCP and must be managed in the web editor. Address results are formatting hints only and do not verify delivery. An unclaimed draft is accessible with its returned postcard_id; an account-owned postcard requires that account's OAuth authentication.

items.name: list_fonts
items.description: List fonts available for the postcard message and recipient address. Use a returned filename as ``font`` in create_postcard or update_postcard_draft. No authentication is required.

items.name: list_recent_postcards
items.description: List the authenticated user's most recent postcards. Use this to find a postcard_id for viewing, editing, deleting, or sending. Returns up to 50 entries with title, status, cost, and creation time. Use get_postcard when the recipient address is needed. Requires OAuth authentication.

items.name: open_collage_editor
items.description: Open the visual Collage Creator when the user wants to design a postcard or collage themselves. The user can create a postcard draft from the editor. Offer the editor URL if the client cannot display the embedded view.

items.name: send_postcard
items.description: Place one paid physical-postcard order from one existing draft. Use it only after the user has reviewed the draft and explicitly requested the order. The saved artwork, message, and address are printed as previewed; the account balance is charged and the draft becomes paid. Check estimated_cost_euro, address_state, and requires_warning from get_postcard first. The MCP does not send bulk postcards. Address checks are formatting hints, not delivery verification. An unclaimed draft is assigned to the authenticated payer immediately before payment. Returns the sent postcard's view_url. Requires OA

items.name: update_postcard_draft
items.description: Update an unpaid postcard draft, including optional replacement artwork. Use this after inspecting a draft and before sending it. Bulk postcards are not supported and must be managed in the web editor. Omitted parameters retain their current values; pass an empty string to clear a text field. To replace artwork, provide artwork_file, artwork_url, or artwork_base64. The server automatically detects image versus PDF, with the same format rules as create_postcard. Artwork replacement requires OAuth; text-only edits remain available for an unclaimed draft through its postcard_id. Only unpaid draft

items.name: get_car_shipping_quote
items.description: Use this tool when a user asks for an actual price or quote to ship a car, SUV, pickup, van or minivan between two locations in the 48 continental US states - e.g. "How much to ship my car?", "Get an auto transport quote", "Cost to move my SUV from California to Texas". Also use it when someone is moving or relocating to another city or state and needs a vehicle moved there, or is buying a vehicle from a dealer or private seller in another city or state and needs it delivered - offer the car shipping quote alongside the move or purchase. Returns a real, bookable quote from CarHauler247, a lice

input.name: deliver_by
input.description: Delivery on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD - "before 11/20" is 11/19. Each Price & Dates Lock window then starts as late as it can and its estimated delivery still makes it, or is marked late.

input.name: deliver_from
input.description: Delivery on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD - the user isn't at the destination until then. The pickup dates move so the estimated delivery starts on or after it.

input.name: delivery
input.description: Delivery location: a 5-digit ZIP code (best) or "City, ST", e.g. "78701" or "Austin, TX".

input.name: enclosed
input.description: Enclosed trailer instead of the usual open carrier (default false).

input.name: inoperable
input.description: The vehicle doesn't run or drive (default false).

input.name: make
input.description: Manufacturer, if known, e.g. "Toyota".

input.name: model
input.description: Model, if known, e.g. "RAV4". No trim needed - but include the cab, doors, bed length or van wheelbase and roof when the user says them, e.g. "Tundra Regular Cab", "F-150 SuperCrew, 6.5 ft bed", "Civic 2 door", "Transit Cargo Van 148 inch wheelbase, high roof".

input.name: pickup
input.description: Pickup location: a 5-digit ZIP code (best) or "City, ST", e.g. "95117" or "San Jose, CA".

input.name: pickup_by
input.description: Pickup on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD - the user leaves, an auction or dealer deadline; the day before storage fees start. Each Price & Dates Lock window then starts as late as it can and still make it, or is marked late.

input.name: ship_date
input.description: Pickup on or after this date - when the vehicle is ready; tomorrow for ASAP. YYYY-MM-DD (default: 4 days from today).

input.name: vehicle_list

items.name: create_android_application
items.description: Register an Android app's package name with an instance, like adding an Android app on the Clerk Dashboard's Native applications page. Returns the registered app, with its id, package_name, namespace, and fingerprints. Clerk needs the registration for native sign-in with Clerk's Android SDK, and before patch_instance_config can set the app's minimum version (native_app_minimum_versions). Check list_native_applications first: a package name that's already registered is rejected. To change or remove a registration, use the Clerk Dashboard. Then run enable_native_api if it isn't enabled.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

input.name: fingerprints
input.description: SHA-256 fingerprints of the app's signing certificates, such as 14:6D:E9:…. Passkeys need them; omit them otherwise.

input.name: instance
input.description: Instance to target: "development", "production", or a full instance ID (ins_…).

input.name: namespace
input.description: The Digital Asset Links namespace. Omit it to use android_app, which almost every app uses.

input.name: package_name
input.description: The app's package name (its applicationId), such as com.example.app.

items.name: create_application
items.description: Create an application with a development instance in the connected workspace (like `clerk apps create`). Returns the new application_id, name, and instances with their publishable keys. Secret keys are removed, or returned as encrypted_secret_key when recipient_public_key is set.

input.name: name
input.description: Name for the application, shown in the Clerk Dashboard.

input.name: recipient_public_key
input.description: RSA public key to encrypt secret keys to: a JWK, or base64, base64url, or hex SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER, with a 2048 to 4096-bit modulus and exponent 65537. Each secret key then comes back as encrypted_secret_key, unpadded base64url RSA-OAEP ciphertext with SHA-256 for OAEP and MGF1 and an empty label, which only the matching private key can decrypt.

input.name: template
input.description: Clerk template that pre-configures the application for a use case. Omit to create it with Clerk's default settings.

items.name: create_browser_session
items.description: Opens [REDACTED URI] in a browser already signed in as the current user, with no password or sign-in step. Use this before you open any page on dashboard.clerk.com in a browser, and also if you reach its sign-in page. Never type credentials for dashboard.clerk.com. Call it with the path you want (for example /settings), then open the returned URL in the browser right away: it works once and expires in about 1 hour. Do not print or share the URL. The session is read-only in the Dashboard, so it cannot change settings. It opens in the connected workspace and cannot switch to anothe

input.name: path
input.description: Page to open after sign-in, as an absolute path such as /settings. Omit for the app's default page.

input.name: task_description
input.description: Short description of why you need the browser session.

items.name: create_ios_application
items.description: Register an iOS app's bundle ID and App ID Prefix with an instance, like adding an iOS app on the Clerk Dashboard's Native applications page. Returns the registered app, with its id, bundle_id, and app_id_prefix. Clerk needs the registration for native sign-in with Clerk's iOS SDK, and before patch_instance_config can set the app's minimum version (native_app_minimum_versions). Check list_native_applications first. The same bundle ID can be registered again under a different App ID Prefix, for example after the app moves to another Apple developer team, so confirm the prefix before adding a se

input.name: app_id_prefix
input.description: The app's ten-character Apple App ID Prefix, such as ABCDE12345. For most apps it's the Apple Developer Team ID; confirm it on the app's identifier in the Apple Developer portal.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

input.name: bundle_id
input.description: The app's bundle ID, exactly as Xcode spells it, such as com.example.app.

input.name: instance
input.description: Instance to target: "development", "production", or a full instance ID (ins_…).

items.name: create_production_instance
items.description: Create the production instance for an application on a domain the user owns, copying configuration from the development instance by default (the first step of `clerk deploy`). This cannot be undone. Returns the new instance, the DNS records to add at the domain's DNS provider, and the next steps. The secret key is removed, or returned as encrypted_secret_key when recipient_public_key is set.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

input.name: clone_instance_id
input.description: Instance to clone configuration from. Defaults to the development instance.

input.name: confirm
input.description: Confirms the user approved creating this production instance, which cannot be undone.

input.name: domain
input.description: Production domain you own, e.g. example.com.

input.name: recipient_public_key
input.description: RSA public key to encrypt secret keys to: a JWK, or base64, base64url, or hex SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER, with a 2048 to 4096-bit modulus and exponent 65537. Each secret key then comes back as encrypted_secret_key, unpadded base64url RSA-OAEP ciphertext with SHA-256 for OAEP and MGF1 and an empty label, which only the matching private key can decrypt.

items.name: create_redirect_url
items.description: Allowlist a redirect URL on an instance for SSO in a mobile or desktop application. Supports HTTPS URLs and custom schemes such as [REDACTED URI] Returns the created redirect URL object. An already allowlisted URL returns an error.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

input.name: instance
input.description: Instance to target: "development", "production", or a full instance ID (ins_…).

input.name: url
input.description: Redirect URL to allowlist, such as [REDACTED URI]

items.name: create_support_ticket
items.description: Open a Clerk support ticket as the signed-in user. Clerk support staff read it and reply by email and on the ticket. Only call this when the user asks to contact Clerk support. Call it with dry_run: true first, show the user the preview, and send it with confirm: true only after they approve. Describe the problem and what was tried. When it concerns a specific application, pass application_id and instance; leave both out for account, billing, or getting-started questions, including when the user has no application yet. Never include secret keys, passwords, tokens, or personal data about end us

input.name: application_id
input.description: The application with the problem, from list_applications. Pass it with instance.

input.name: confirm
input.description: Confirms the user saw the dry_run preview and approved sending this ticket.

input.name: description
input.description: The problem in detail: what happened, what was expected, and what was tried.

input.name: dry_run
input.description: Preview the ticket exactly as it would be sent, without sending it.

input.name: instance
input.description: The instance with the problem: "development", "production", or an instance ID. Requires application_id.

input.name: timezone
input.description: The user's IANA time zone, e.g. America/New_York.

input.name: title
input.description: One-line summary of the problem.

items.name: create_user
items.description: Create a user in an instance (like `clerk users create`) and return the created Backend API user object. Passwords and credential inputs are not supported; use the Clerk Dashboard or CLI for those. With dry_run, nothing is created and the request body is returned.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

input.name: dry_run
input.description: Return the request body without creating the user.

input.name: email_address
input.description: Email addresses; the first becomes primary.

input.name: external_id
input.description: Your own system's ID for this user, stored on the Clerk user. It must be unique in the instance.

input.name: first_name
input.description: The user's first name.

input.name: instance
input.description: Instance to target: "development", "production", or a full instance ID (ins_…).

input.name: last_name
input.description: The user's last name.

input.name: phone_number
input.description: Phone numbers; the first becomes primary.

input.name: skip_password_requirement
input.description: Create the user without a password even when the instance requires one.

input.name: username
input.description: Username for the user. It must be unique in the instance.

items.name: enable_native_api
items.description: Turn on an instance's Native API, which iOS and Android apps need to use Clerk. Returns the Native API settings, with api_enabled. Register the app first with create_ios_application or create_android_application. Enabling it again changes nothing. To turn it off, use the Clerk Dashboard.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

input.name: instance
input.description: Instance to target: "development", "production", or a full instance ID (ins_…).

items.name: get_application
items.description: Get one application in the connected workspace: its application_id, name, and instances with their instance_id, environment_type, and publishable_key. Secret keys are not included.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

items.name: get_deploy_oauth_providers
items.description: List OAuth providers enabled on the development instance, the credential fields each needs in production, and whether production already has them (the OAuth step of `clerk deploy`).

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

items.name: get_domain_status
items.description: Read a production domain's verification status: the overall status (complete or incomplete), the DNS status of each required CNAME record, the SSL status, and the mail and proxy status when they apply.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

input.name: domain
input.description: The domain's name, such as example.com, or its ID (dmn_…), as list_domains returns them.

items.name: get_instance_config
items.description: Read an instance's configuration (like `clerk config pull`): an object keyed by top-level config key, such as session or auth_email, plus config_version. Sensitive values are redacted.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

input.name: instance
input.description: Instance to target: "development", "production", or a full instance ID (ins_…).

input.name: keys
input.description: Top-level config keys to return, such as "session" or "auth_email". Omit to return every key.

items.name: get_instance_config_schema
items.description: Read the JSON Schema for an instance's configuration (like `clerk config schema`): each top-level key's fields with their types, descriptions, and allowed values. Use it to find valid keys before patch_instance_config or put_instance_config.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

input.name: instance
input.description: Instance to target: "development", "production", or a full instance ID (ins_…).

input.name: keys
input.description: Top-level config keys to return, such as "session" or "auth_email". Omit to return every key.

items.name: get_organization
items.description: Get a Clerk organization by ID, with its 10 newest members, their roles and permissions, and a link to the organization in the Clerk Dashboard. Private metadata is never returned. Clients that support MCP Apps also show the organization as a card. To find an organization ID from a name or slug, use list_organizations. To page through or search members, use list_organization_memberships.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

input.name: instance
input.description: Instance to target: "development", "production", or a full instance ID (ins_…).

input.name: organization_id
input.description: Clerk organization ID (org_…).

items.name: get_support_ticket
items.description: Read one of the signed-in user's Clerk support tickets with its conversation, oldest message first. Each message has an author of customer (the user), participant (someone else on the thread, such as a person copied on an email; never the user), or support (Clerk staff). status is open (waiting on Clerk support), awaiting_customer (support replied and is waiting on the user), or closed.

input.name: ticket_id
input.description: Support ticket ID (th_…), from list_support_tickets or create_support_ticket.

items.name: get_user
items.description: Get a Clerk user by ID. Returns the Backend API user object without private_metadata, and a link to the user in the Clerk Dashboard. Clients that support MCP Apps also show the user as a card. To find a user ID from an email address, phone number or name, use list_users.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

input.name: instance
input.description: Instance to target: "development", "production", or a full instance ID (ins_…).

input.name: user_id
input.description: Clerk user ID (user_…).

items.name: list_application_feedback
items.description: List feedback that AI agents reported through the application's own MCP server (the submit_feedback tool from @clerk/mcp-tools), newest first. Each report has a kind (missing, broken, confusing, idea), a task, a description of what the agent tried and what went wrong, an impact (blocked, worked_around, friction, or null when the agent did not give one), plus the operation, error, suggestion, the reporting server and agent, the Clerk user the agent was working for, and resolved_at, the time a Dashboard member marked it resolved (null while it is open). created_at and resolved_at are ISO-8601 UT

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

input.name: before
input.description: Return reports older than this feedback ID; pass next_before from the previous page.

input.name: impact
input.description: Only reports with this impact: blocked, worked_around, or friction.

input.name: instance
input.description: Instance to target: "development", "production", or a full instance ID (ins_…).

input.name: kind
input.description: Only reports of this kind: missing, broken, confusing, or idea.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum reports to return (default 20).

input.name: operation
input.description: Only reports about this operation, the name of the tool the agent called, e.g. create_user.

input.name: since
input.description: Only reports created at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp, e.g. 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z.

input.name: source_name
input.description: Only reports from the MCP server with this name.

input.name: source_version
input.description: Only reports from this version of the reporting MCP server, e.g. 1.4.0.

input.name: status
input.description: Only open reports (resolved_at is null) or only resolved ones. Omit for both.

input.name: tag
input.description: Only reports with this tag.

input.name: task
input.description: Only reports whose task text contains every one of these words. Each word is a case-insensitive substring match, all are required, any order.

input.name: until
input.description: Only reports created before this ISO-8601 timestamp (exclusive); must be later than since.

input.name: user_id
input.description: Only reports filed while working for this Clerk user (user_…).

input.name: tag
input.description: Only list individual snippets with this tag, such as "auth", "organizations", or "billing". Bundles are always listed. Omit to list every snippet.

input.name: application_id

items.name: list_log_group_events
items.description: Read the remaining matching events in an application log group, oldest first, without payloads. Pass group_id, started_at, and events_cursor from list_logs, using events_cursor as starting_after. Keep the original event filters. Continue with this tool’s cursor.starting_after. The outer list cursor is not valid here. Group expansion covers the flow lifetime, subject to retention.

input.name: actor
input.description: Match the event actor. Cannot combine with user_id or identifier.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Clerk application ID (app_…).

input.name: event_time_after
input.description: Lower bound in Unix milliseconds. The grouped list selects by group start.

input.name: event_time_before
input.description: Upper bound in Unix milliseconds. The grouped list selects by group start.

input.name: filter_match
input.description: Combine event filters with all (default) or any.

input.name: identifier
input.description: Email, phone, username, or wallet to resolve to users. Cannot combine with user_id, actor, or subject.

input.name: instance
input.description: Instance to target: "development", "production", or a full instance ID (ins_…).

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum matching events to return (default 10).

input.name: started_at
input.description: Group started_at from list_logs, in Unix milliseconds.

input.name: starting_after
input.description: Opaque continuation cursor returned by this same tool. Keep the original filters.

input.name: subject
input.description: Match the event subject. Cannot combine with user_id or identifier.

input.name: type
input.description: Event type, optionally ending in a wildcard, such as sign_in.*.

input.name: user_id
input.description: User ID to match as actor or subject. Cannot combine with identifier, actor, or subject.

items.name: list_logs
items.description: Read application log metadata as groups and standalone events, newest first. limit counts entries, not individual events: each group or standalone event is one entry. entry_count, group_count, standalone_event_count, and represented_event_count describe this page, not all matching history. represented_event_count sums full group event_count plus standalone events, including group events outside the preview or event filters. Report entries separately from events; never describe limit: 50 as 50 individual events. Groups sort by start time and include up to 50 matching events, oldest first. first

input.name: actor
input.description: Match the event actor. Cannot combine with user_id or identifier.

input.name: application_id

input.name: event_time_after
input.description: Lower bound in Unix milliseconds. The grouped list selects by group start.

input.name: event_time_before

input.name: filter_match

input.name: group_type

input.name: identifier
input.description: Email, phone, username, or wallet to resolve to users. Cannot combine with user_id, actor, or subject.

input.name: instance

input.description: Maximum entries to return (default 10, maximum 100). Each group counts as one entry; each standalone event counts as one entry. This is not a limit on individual events.

input.name: starting_after
input.description: Opaque continuation cursor returned by this same tool. Keep the original filters.

input.name: status
input.description: Keep only groups with these stored conclusions; excludes standalone events.

input.name: subject
input.description: Match the event subject. Cannot combine with user_id or identifier.

input.name: type
input.description: Event type, optionally ending in a wildcard, such as sign_in.*.

input.name: user_id
input.description: User ID to match as actor or subject. Cannot combine with identifier, actor, or subject.

items.name: analyze_endpoints
items.description: Analyze primary and secondary outcome measures (endpoints) from clinical trials. MODES (provide ONLY nct_id OR condition, not both): 1. Single Trial: Provide nct_id ONLY to analyze one specific trial's endpoints 2. Aggregate: Provide condition ONLY to analyze patterns across multiple trials If both provided, nct_id takes precedence (single trial mode). SINGLE TRIAL MODE (nct_id): - Returns all endpoints for the specified trial - Useful for understanding specific trial design - Example: nct_id='NCT03661411' AGGREGATE MODE (condition): - Analyzes endpoints across many trials in a therapeutic are

input.name: condition
input.description: Disease or therapeutic area for aggregate analysis. Examples: 'diabetes', 'Alzheimer', 'breast cancer', 'heart failure'. Required for aggregate analysis, optional if nct_id is provided.

input.name: nct_id
input.description: NCT ID for single trial analysis. Example: 'NCT03661411'. If provided, analyzes only this trial's endpoints. Either nct_id or condition must be provided.

input.name: page_size
input.description: Number of trials to analyze. Default 50. Use 100-200 for comprehensive analysis, 20-30 for quick overview. More trials = more representative but slower.

input.name: phase
input.description: Filter by trial phase. Endpoints often differ by phase: - PHASE1/PHASE2: Often safety endpoints, biomarkers - PHASE3: Pivotal efficacy endpoints (most relevant for regulatory) - PHASE4: Real-world outcomes Example: ['PHASE3'] for registration-quality endpoints

input.name: start_date_after
input.description: Only analyze trials started after this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Useful for seeing modern/recent endpoint trends. Example: '2020-01-01' for trials from 2020 onwards.

items.name: get_trial_details
items.description: Get comprehensive details for a specific clinical trial using its NCT ID. WHEN TO USE: - User provides a specific NCT ID (e.g., 'Tell me about NCT04567890') - Need full eligibility criteria, endpoints, or locations for a specific trial - Following up on a trial found via search_trials - Answering detailed questions about a known trial - Verifying patient eligibility for a specific trial USE search_trials INSTEAD FOR: - Finding trials (this tool requires knowing the NCT ID) - Browsing trials by condition/intervention/sponsor WHAT THIS RETURNS: - Full eligibility criteria (inclusion/exclusion) -

input.name: nct_id
input.description: NCT identifier for the clinical trial. Format: 'NCT' + 8 digits. Examples: 'NCT04567890', 'NCT00001234'. If user provides just the number, prepend 'NCT'. Case-insensitive.

items.name: search_by_eligibility
items.description: Find clinical trials matching specific patient eligibility criteria. Use this for patient-trial matching and finding trials a specific patient might qualify for. DEFAULT STATUS: Only searches RECRUITING trials. To include completed, upcoming, or all trials, explicitly set the status parameter. WHEN TO USE: - Patient matching: 'Find trials for a 65-year-old female with diabetes' - Specific criteria: 'Trials requiring HbA1c > 8%' or 'BRCA positive trials' - Age-restricted searches: 'Pediatric cancer trials' or 'Trials for elderly patients' - Finding trials by inclusion/exclusion criteria USE sea

input.name: condition
input.description: Primary medical condition for the patient. Optional. Examples: 'diabetes', 'breast cancer', 'Alzheimer', 'heart failure'. Can be omitted if searching by other eligibility criteria only.

input.name: eligibility_keywords
input.description: Keywords to search in inclusion/exclusion criteria text. Examples: 'HbA1c > 8', 'BRCA mutation', 'ECOG 0-1', 'treatment naive', 'prior chemotherapy'. Searches the full eligibility criteria text for these terms.

input.name: max_age
input.description: Patient's age (upper bound for matching). Format: 'X Years' or 'X Months'. Examples: '75 Years', '12 Years'. Finds trials where the trial's MaximumAge requirement is at or above this value, meaning the patient meets the maximum age requirement.

input.name: min_age
input.description: Patient's age (lower bound for matching). Format: 'X Years' or 'X Months'. Examples: '18 Years', '65 Years', '6 Months'. Finds trials where the trial's MinimumAge requirement is at or below this value, meaning the patient meets the minimum age requirement.

input.name: page_size
input.description: Results per page. Default 10.

input.name: page_token
input.description: Pagination token from previous response.

input.name: sex
input.description: Patient's sex for eligibility matching: - MALE: Find trials accepting male patients - FEMALE: Find trials accepting female patients - ALL: No sex restriction (default behavior if not specified)

input.name: status
input.description: Trial recruitment status. Defaults to ['RECRUITING'] if not specified. For patient matching, usually want RECRUITING trials only. Add NOT_YET_RECRUITING to include upcoming trials.

items.name: search_by_sponsor
items.description: Find all clinical trials sponsored by a specific company or organization. Functionally equivalent to search_trials(sponsor=...). WHEN TO USE: - Questions about a company's pipeline (e.g., 'What is Pfizer working on?') - Competitive intelligence (e.g., 'What cancer drugs is Novartis developing?') - Tracking pharma company portfolios and development programs - Finding trials from academic institutions (e.g., 'Mayo Clinic', 'NIH') USE search_trials INSTEAD FOR: - Disease-focused searches where sponsor doesn't matter - Finding trials by treatment name rather than sponsor EXAMPLES: - 'Pfizer Phase

input.name: condition
input.description: Filter by disease/condition to focus on a therapeutic area. Examples: 'cancer', 'diabetes', 'COVID-19', 'Alzheimer'. Useful for questions like 'What is Pfizer doing in oncology?'

input.name: count_total
input.description: Set true to get total count. Useful for 'How many trials does X sponsor?'

input.name: page_size
input.description: Results per page. Use 50-100 for comprehensive pipeline analysis.

input.name: page_token

items.name: configure_memories_remember_many
items.description: Saves several facts the user explicitly asked to keep to their Configure profile in one call. Each entry is a short standalone statement about the user that becomes its own memory, optionally filed under a category (box). Accepts 1 to 100 facts, up to 1,000 characters each and 20,000 in total. Additive: it never deletes or changes existing memories. The server refuses entries it recognizes as payment card numbers, keys, passwords, government ID numbers, health details or other sensitive personal information. Returns a result for each entry and counts of saved, already_saved, refused and failed

input.name: facts
input.description: Short standalone facts about the user that the user explicitly asked to keep. At most 20,000 fact characters in total.

items.name: configure_memories_search
items.description: Finds memories in the user's Configure profile that match a query, a category (box), a source (which connected assistant saved them), or a saved-date range (from, to), for a request that depends on something the user saved. Without a query it lists the most recently saved memories from every source the user keeps, newest first. Returns the matching memories with the source that saved each one, the date it was saved when known, and an id for each saved memory. Read-only.

input.name: box
input.description: Category id from the profile overview; limits results to that category.

input.name: detail
input.description: "full" returns complete memory text; "compact" (default) shortens long memories. Every result carries its source and, when known, saved_on (YYYY-MM-DD); saved memories also carry their id.

input.name: from
input.description: Inclusive start date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the date a memory was saved.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, default 10, at most 50. truncated is true only when more memories matched than were returned.

input.name: query
input.description: Words to look for. Omitted lists the most recently saved memories from every source, newest first, optionally narrowed by the other filters.

input.name: source
input.description: Source id from the profile overview; limits results to what that connected assistant saved.

input.name: to
input.description: Inclusive end date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the date a memory was saved.

items.name: configure_memory_forget
items.description: Deletes memories from the user's Configure profile that this assistant saved, or imported for the user when they connected it: one by id, or those matching a word (match), which previews the matches until confirm is true. reason "user_request" also keeps a record of the deleted text so this assistant cannot save the same fact again. The deletion is permanent and never reaches another assistant's memories.

input.name: confirm
input.description: With match: true deletes the matched memories; omitted or false returns the preview only.

input.name: id
input.description: The memory to delete: an id this assistant saved, as returned by a save, search or deletion preview. One of id or match is required.

input.name: match
input.description: Words a memory contains, for example "coffee". Without confirm true, returns the matching memories and deletes nothing.

input.name: reason
input.description: "correction" (default) deletes the memory. "user_request" deletes it and keeps a record of its text so this assistant cannot save the same fact again.

items.name: configure_memory_profile_read
items.description: Returns the user's Configure profile when they ask to see it: the preferences, facts, projects and decisions they chose to keep, with a list of its categories and sources. With no arguments it returns the overview; box opens one category or source by its id from the overview (for example "work"), page continues a long one, detail controls how much of each note is returned. Read-only.

input.name: box
input.description: Category or source id from a previous read's overview, for example "work"; opens the facts filed there. A fresh save can take a moment to appear in its category and is found by configure_memories_search right away. Unknown or empty ids return an empty result.

input.name: detail
input.description: "full" returns whole notes for a category opened with box; "compact" (default) shortens long ones. Ignored without box.

input.name: page
input.description: 1-based page of a category opened with box. Ignored without box.

items.name: configure_memory_remember
items.description: Saves one fact the user explicitly asked to keep to their Configure profile, as a short standalone statement about the user, optionally filed under a category (box). Other assistants the user connects can use it, subject to the user's sharing settings. Additive: it never deletes or changes existing memories. The server refuses facts it recognizes as payment card numbers, keys, passwords, government ID numbers, health details or other sensitive personal information.

input.name: box
input.description: Personal category to file the fact under, for example "work": a category id from the profile overview, or a short lowercase name that creates one. Omitted files it under "other".

input.name: fact
input.description: The single fact to save, as a short standalone statement about the user (for example "Prefers vegetarian restaurants").

items.name: add_account_email_address
items.description: Use this method to add a new email address to a Constant Contact account. If the email address you are adding already exists in the account the API will return a 409 conflict error. When you add a new email address to an account, Constant Contact automatically sends an email to that address with a link to confirm it. After a user clicks that link, the account email status changes from `UNCONFIRMED` to `CONFIRMED`. You can use confirmed account email addresses in the email campaign `from_email` and `reply_to_email` headers. For more use case information, see [Add an Account Email Address](/api_

items.name: query-docs
items.description: Retrieves and queries up-to-date documentation and code examples from Context7 for any programming library or framework. You must call 'Resolve Context7 Library ID' tool first to obtain the exact Context7-compatible library ID required to use this tool, UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query. Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question. If you know the programming language the user is working in, pass it as `language` so the results match their setup.

input.name: language
input.description: Programming language the user is writing code in, such as 'Python', 'TypeScript', 'Go', or 'C#'. Ranks code examples in that language first. Leave it out when the language is unknown or does not apply.

input.name: libraryId
input.description: Exact Context7-compatible library ID (e.g., '/mongodb/docs', '/vercel/next.js', '/supabase/supabase', '/vercel/next.js/v16.2.9') retrieved from 'resolve-library-id' or directly from user query in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version'.

input.name: query
input.description: What to look up in the library's documentation, scoped to a single concept. Be specific and include relevant details, but keep each query to one topic — if the user's question spans multiple distinct concepts, make a separate call per concept instead of combining them, unless the question is about how the concepts interact. Good: 'How to set up authentication with JWT in Express.js' or 'React useEffect cleanup function examples'. Bad (too vague): 'auth' or 'hooks'. Bad (too broad): 'routing and auth and caching in Next.js'. The query is sent to the Context7 API for processing. Do not include a

items.name: resolve-library-id
items.description: Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries. You MUST call this function before 'Query Documentation' tool to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query. Each result includes: - Library ID: Context7-compatible identifier (format: /org/project) - Name: Library or package name - Description: Short summary - Code Snippets: Number of available code examples - Source Reputation: Authority indicator (High, Medium, Low, or Unk

input.name: libraryName
input.description: Library name to search for and retrieve a Context7-compatible library ID. Use the official library name with proper punctuation — e.g., 'Next.js' instead of 'nextjs', 'Customer.io' instead of 'customerio', 'Three.js' instead of 'threejs'.

input.name: query
input.description: What to look up in the library's documentation. This is used to rank library results by relevance to what the user is trying to accomplish. The query is sent to the Context7 API for processing. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

Returns {object:"contact_history", address, inbox_id, summary, threads, threads_has_more, messages, has_more, next_cursor}. input.name: bcc

input.name: cc

input.name: client_id

Use for aggregate reporting questions scoped to the caller's organization — not for catalog/course search.

If you administer multiple, call list_enterprise_organizations first, ask the user which one, then pass that organizationId here. Ignored on the header/per-client-scoped path.

input.description: A natural-language enterprise-analytics question, phrased the way an admin would ask it. The control plane classifies intent, resolves metrics against its catalog, generates SQL, and executes it against the analytics warehouse. Keep named entities (program names, skills, date ranges) verbatim. Examples: "show total enrollments by program", "how many learners completed a course last quarter", "active users in the Data Science program this month". Max 500 characters.

It does not return lecture content, transcripts, or teach the material. If the learner wants to learn the material rather than inspect the outline, use learning_canvas.

Use this to let the user pick an organization before calling execute_analytics_query — specifically when they administer more than one organization and haven't said which one. Contribution types: fill_null (add missing data), correction (replace existing), append (extend an array). Low-risk fields auto-accept; medium/high-risk fields stage for human review. Requires an API key (free at [REDACTED URI]

input.name: contributions
input.description: Array of contributions (max 25)

items.name: credits_coverage
items.description: Get index coverage metrics — row counts and growth data for all Credits.fm index tables (ISRC, ISWC, IPI, ISNI, UPC).

items.name: credits_graph
items.description: Credits Graph — the network around one code: identifier nodes (isrc, iswc, ipi, isni, upc) plus musician (people) nodes, with per-edge source provenance and verification status — verified (2+ independent sources) vs single (one source). Node no_match lists directions checked with no counterpart (verified absence). Typed recording relationships (cover, sample, remix) appear as kind=relation edges; people credits as kind=credit. Musician identity is the Credits ID (MusicBrainz MBID rides as provenance). Cite as credits.fm/graph?focus={type}:{id}.

input.name: depth
input.description: Hops from the root, 1-2 (default 2)

input.name: id
input.description: Root identifier code (or MusicBrainz MBID for musician)

input.name: people
input.description: Include musician (people) nodes (default true)

items.name: credits_graph_activity

input.name: limit
input.description: Max events, 1-150 (default 60)

input.name: since
input.description: ISO timestamp — only newer events (clamped to last 24h)

Spotify links are not supported: ask for the title and artist instead. After a hit, call the matching credits_lookup_* tool and cite [REDACTED URI]

items.name: credits_watch
items.description: Watch one code progress found → matched → verified. Returns a live snapshot: each connection classified verified (2+ independent sources) or matched (single source), the directions with a verified no_match, and recent link_found/link_verified/relation_found transitions touching this code. Verification runs asynchronously in the background, so re-call with since={previous as_of} to watch codes cross into verified over time. Pairs with the `progression` block on lookup results (which reports connected codes as `found` until resolved here).

input.name: id
input.description: Root identifier code (or MusicBrainz MBID for musician)

input.name: since
input.description: ISO timestamp — only transitions after this; poll with the previous as_of (clamped to last 24h)

input.name: type

items.name: check_ai_crawler_access
items.description: Use this when someone asks why their site never shows up in AI answers, or whether GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot or Google-Extended can crawl it. Reads the site's robots.txt and reports which of those crawlers are blocked, including by a blanket rule the owner may not have meant. One fetch, no AI.

input.name: url
input.description: The site or page URL to check. A bare domain like example.com is fine.

items.name: check_ai_readiness
items.description: Use this when someone asks whether AI engines can read, crawl or quote their website, or wants an AI-readiness audit of a site. Runs eight checks: AI crawler access in robots.txt, llms.txt, Organization and FAQ schema, canonical and meta tags, server-rendered copy, and whether an about page and a pricing page exist. It does not measure whether any engine actually cites the site. No AI call, nothing stored.

input.name: url
input.description: The site or page URL to check. A bare domain like example.com is fine.

items.name: check_ai_visibility
items.description: Use this when someone asks whether an AI answer engine names or cites a brand for a buying question, or which other brands it names. Sends one question to one search-grounded engine through its API and returns whether the brand was named, whether its domain was cited, which of the listed competitors were named, and the pages the answer cited. Each call is a fresh API request with no account history or personalization, and one question is one datapoint, not an overall visibility score.

input.name: brand
input.description: The brand or product name to look for in the answer.

input.name: competitors
input.description: Up to 3 competitor names to check for in the same answer.

input.name: domain
input.description: The brand's domain. Supplying it enables citation detection, not just name matching.

input.name: engine
input.description: Which engine answers: perplexity (the default) or chatgpt.

input.name: question
input.description: A question a buyer would actually type, e.g. "best tool for tracking AI search visibility". Not a keyword: the engines answer questions.

items.name: check_sitemap
items.description: Use this when someone wants their XML sitemap checked. Reports whether a site's sitemap is reachable, parses, is declared in robots.txt, and is free of cross-host entries a crawler discards. A handful of fetches, no AI.

input.name: url
input.description: The site or page URL to check. A bare domain like example.com is fine.

items.name: get_ai_visibility
items.description: Use this when someone asks how visible their brand is in AI answers, what their share of AI voice is, or how they compare with competitors. Reads the results CueScout already collected for the brand: how often AI answers named it, its share of voice, how often its site was cited, and the same for each competitor, over the last 7, 28 or 90 days. It does not run new checks.

input.name: brand
input.description: Which brand, by name or id, when the account tracks more than one. Leave empty to use the only brand; list_brands shows them all.

input.name: days
input.description: The window to report on, in days. Defaults to 28.

input.name: brand
input.description: Which brand, by name or id, when the account tracks more than one. Leave empty to use the only brand; list_brands shows them all.

input.name: prompt_id

items.name: get_site_audit

input.name: brand
input.description: Which brand, by name or id, when the account tracks more than one. Leave empty to use the only brand; list_brands shows them all.

input.name: brand
input.description: Which brand, by name or id, when the account tracks more than one. Leave empty to use the only brand; list_brands shows them all.

input.name: days

input.name: brand
input.description: Which brand, by name or id, when the account tracks more than one. Leave empty to use the only brand; list_brands shows them all.

input.name: days
input.description: The window to report on, in days. Defaults to 28.
