items.description: Interactive print preview of a cleaned-up web page.

items.name: create_map_poster
items.description: Use when the user wants a map poster, a city or street map print, map wall art or a map gift of a real place. Builds the poster in the printm.app editor from real OpenStreetMap data, so streets, rivers and coastlines are accurate and it exports print-ready at up to A1 (an illustrated or generated picture of a map would invent the streets). Sets up place, style, paper size, caption, contour lines and 3D terrain. Free, no account. Give either a place name that has its own page, or lat and lng (any place on Earth), or country_code for a country-silhouette poster. Returns the editor URL to hand to

input.name: contours
input.description: Elevation contour lines.

input.name: coords
input.description: Third caption line. Leave out and the app prints the centre coordinates.

input.name: country_code
input.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, e.g. JPN — makes a country-silhouette poster instead of a street map.

input.name: dpi
input.description: Export resolution; 300 is print quality. Larger posters are viewed from further away and need less (see /poster-size-calculator).

input.name: height_cm
input.description: Custom height in cm (5-500).

input.name: labels
input.description: Script for place names on the map.

input.name: lat
input.description: Latitude in decimal degrees. Required unless the place is known or country_code is used.

input.name: lng
input.description: Longitude in decimal degrees.

input.name: place
input.description: Place name; used for the caption and, if we have a page for it, for the coordinates.

input.name: size
input.description: Paper size; A1 is the largest.

input.name: style
input.description: Map style id; see list_map_styles.

input.name: subtitle
input.description: Second caption line, e.g. the country or a date.

input.name: terrain_3d
input.description: 3D shaded terrain.

input.name: title
input.description: First caption line printed on the poster.

input.name: width_cm
input.description: Custom width in cm (5-500); use with height_cm instead of size.

input.name: zoom
input.description: 11 whole city, 13 a few neighbourhoods, 15 streets. Default 12.

items.name: find_place
items.description: Search the 324 cities and 205 countries that have their own page on printm.app. Returns coordinates, the page URL and a poster image. Places not listed still work — pass lat and lng to create_map_poster.

input.name: query
input.description: Place name or part of it.

items.name: list_map_styles
items.description: The 25 map styles available, with their ids for create_map_poster.

items.name: ads_create_account
items.description: Set up a self-serve Product Hunt ad account for the signed-in user, when ads_get_context lists none. Give what they promote: post_id of a Product Hunt launch they make or are on the team of, or website_url. budget_band is their approximate total budget. Set agency (and client_name) when booking for a client. The account's confirmed Product Hunt email becomes the contact and can sign in to Ads Manager. Product Hunt's ads team sees the request. A returning self-serve buyer gets their existing account back. This creates no campaign, draft, or payment. Next, call ads_start_draft with the returned

items.name: ads_get_campaign
items.description: Read an authorized campaign, a page of its permitted budgets, and its self-serve portal creative state (slots, associated launch selection, and variant controls) when your membership reaches the campaign's asset request. live means an active, unpaused budget with live placements; daily limits, targeting, and auctions still affect delivery, and draft budgets never serve. creative is null when no current portal asset request is reachable. Give the user preview_url to see the ad on the real Product Hunt homepage. Commercial terms and billing details are not exposed; delivery results are in ads_ge

items.name: ads_get_context
items.description: List ad accounts accessible through your current portal membership. Follow next_after_id even when a page is empty. Every account can manage drafts and campaigns; access is always advertiser. With none, offer ads_create_account.

items.name: ads_get_draft
items.description: Read your current unfinished ad composer draft, available placement options, and text and image field limits. Requires account-wide portal access. A null draft means no saved work. Budgets and minimums are in whole USD; these are draft choices, not a price quote or reservation. A managed account's draft (mode request) is a campaign request with no budgets or checkout, so its min_budget is 0. Billing stays in the browser and is omitted here. draft.variants lists additional creative variants, whose creative_changes carry their variant_key; draft.launch is the linked Product Hunt launch, set with

items.name: ads_get_performance
items.description: Read delivery results for an ad account you can access: impressions, clicks, CTR, CPM and spend in USD as totals and per campaign, ad type and creative, plus a daily series. Pass campaign_id for one campaign. Figures come from the advertiser portal's report, refreshed about hourly, over the same history as ads_list_campaigns (usually campaigns active in about the last 12 months). Spend is delivered value (impressions at the booked CPM) capped at each booking's budget; it is not an invoice. Totals, campaigns, ad types and creatives always cover the whole report; days, start_date, end_date and b

input.name: breakdown
input.description: Split each day of the daily series by ad_type or by creative; creative rows carry the id of an entry in creatives. none returns day totals only.

input.name: days
input.description: Days in the daily series, ending on end_date; 30 when no dates are passed. Use instead of start_date and end_date.

input.name: end_date
input.description: Last day of the daily series, YYYY-MM-DD in Pacific time, inclusive. Defaults to the last reported day.

input.name: start_date
input.description: First day of the daily series, YYYY-MM-DD in Pacific time, inclusive. Defaults to the first reported day.

items.name: ads_list_campaigns
items.description: List campaigns reachable through your current membership in an ad account. Like the advertiser portal, it leaves out campaigns that ended before the account's visible history begins (usually about 12 months ago). Use ads_get_campaign for authorized budget schedules, delivery status, and editable creative slots.

items.name: ads_prepare_checkout
items.description: Check whether your self-serve ad draft is ready to pay for and quote what checkout will book. Requires account-wide portal access. Pass write_revision as expected_revision. Managed request drafts are rejected. This never charges, holds a card, accepts terms, or submits anything: fix blocking_errors with ads_update_draft (uploading images via ads_prepare_image first), then give the buyer checkout_url to review the terms and pay in the browser. Totals over the card limit use payment_method ach, paid by bank or invoice in the browser. Amounts are whole USD.

items.name: ads_prepare_image
items.description: Prepare an image for an ad draft field (draft_id, kind and asset_kind) or for an existing campaign image slot (campaign_id and slot_id), checked against the returned constraints. Preparing does not change the draft or campaign: once status is ready, attach it with ads_update_draft creative_changes image_id (with a variant_key for a variant) or ads_update_campaign slot_changes image_id. Send the bytes one of three ways: 1. source_url, when the image is already at a public URL. 2. For a local file, prefer the upload: call without source_url or content, then POST the file as multipart field file

input.name: campaign_id
input.description: The campaign, with slot_id from ads_get_campaign creative.slots. Not with draft_id.

input.name: content
input.description: Base64 image bytes from a tool such as base64, at most 3 MB decoded, without a data: prefix; line breaks are ignored. Not with source_url. Your client may allow less than 3 MB; if it rejects the call, send a smaller image.

input.name: draft_id
input.description: The draft, with kind and asset_kind from its image_fields. Not with campaign_id.

input.name: idempotency_key
input.description: Names this image for this account and connection; reuse it only with the same target and source_url. Retry with the same key to get the same image, a fresh ticket, or another try at content after a failure; a ready image accepts only its same bytes.

input.name: source_url
input.description: Public HTTP or HTTPS image URL the server downloads. Not with content.

items.name: ads_start_draft
items.description: Start an empty ad composer draft or return your current unfinished draft without changing it. Requires account-wide portal access. Other members' drafts are never returned. This saves no campaign, payment, submission, or live creative. Use ads_update_draft to fill it in. Repeating this call resumes your current open draft. Add images with ads_prepare_image. Finish checkout in the browser; a managed account's draft (mode request) has no checkout and is sent to the ads team from the browser. Give the user preview_url to see the ad on the real Product Hunt homepage.

items.name: ads_submit_campaign
items.description: Submit an existing campaign's staged creative slot and associated launch changes for review. Requires editable portal access for the campaign. It always takes two calls, and only the second one submits. 1. Call without confirmation_token. Nothing is submitted; the result is outcome needs_confirmation with preview (the slot_changes and launch_change to send), side_effects, warnings for empty required slots, and a confirmation_token valid for 15 minutes. 2. Show the user the preview and side_effects and get their explicit confirmation. Then call again with confirmation_token and without preview.

input.name: confirmation_token
input.description: confirmation_token from the needs_confirmation result; send it only after the user approved that preview. Empty means omitted.

input.name: preview
input.description: True only previews, as omitting confirmation_token does. Cannot be combined with confirmation_token.

items.name: ads_update_campaign
items.description: Edit an existing campaign's self-serve creative slots, associated Product Hunt launch, or creative variants. Requires editable portal access for the campaign. Commercial terms (name, budgets, dates, placements, pause state) are not editable here. - Edits apply directly (outcome applied) and stay staged until ads_submit_campaign submits them; call it when the user is ready to submit. - Removing a live or submitted variant, or passing preview true, changes nothing and returns outcome needs_confirmation with preview, side_effects and a confirmation_token valid for 15 minutes. Show the user and re

input.name: confirmation_token
input.description: confirmation_token from the needs_confirmation result; send it only after the user approved that preview.

input.name: expected_revision
input.description: creative.write_revision from ads_get_campaign. On a conflict, read ads_get_campaign again and reconcile before retrying.

input.name: preview
input.description: True changes nothing and returns needs_confirmation with a preview. Cannot be combined with confirmation_token.

items.name: ads_update_draft
items.description: Save only the changes the user requested to their unfinished ad composer draft. Requires account-wide portal access. Omitted fields and content added in the browser stay saved. This never submits, publishes, charges, or changes a live campaign. Checkout happens in the browser, where a request-mode draft is sent to the ads team instead. Give the user preview_url to see the ad on the real Product Hunt homepage.

input.name: expected_revision
input.description: write_revision from the draft. On a conflict or an uncertain retry, read ads_get_draft and reconcile before saving again.

items.name: find_investable_startups
items.description: Find launches from a date window that Product Hunt's proprietary model ranks as likely to raise a Series A within two years of launch. Use it to surface promising startups; it is not investment advice. When to use: "promising startups that launched last month", "which recent launches look fundable", "the strongest new YC startups", or any request to shortlist new startups by potential. For a plain, unranked list of recent launches, use search_products instead. Only launches in the model's Top 10% are returned, strongest first. series_a_band ranks the launch against all Product Hunt launches, f

input.name: category_slug
input.description: Filter by category slug. Use get_categories to discover valid slugs and pick the most specific matching one (e.g. "ai-dictation-apps" for dictation queries, not the broader parent).

input.name: cursor
input.description: next_cursor from the previous response, unchanged, with the same other arguments. Omit for the first page.

input.name: launched_after
input.description: Earliest launch date, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Set only when the user named a window; otherwise omit (default: 30 days before launched_before). launched_after and launched_before can be at most one year apart.

input.name: launched_before
input.description: Latest launch date, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Set only when the user named a window; otherwise omit (default: today).

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of startups (default: 10).

input.name: query
input.description: A topic or audience to narrow the shortlist, as a short phrase such as "voice AI", "consumer social app" or "healthcare software". One topic per call. Matched by meaning against what each product does and who it is for; a launch whose name or tagline contains every word also matches.

input.name: yc_only
input.description: Only startups Product Hunt has matched to a Y Combinator company. Set it only when the user asked for YC companies.

items.name: get_alternatives
items.description: Find alternatives to one Product Hunt product, most similar first: products that do the same job, without the product itself. product takes a product's slug, name or Product Hunt URL; the response names the product it matched, so check it is the one the user meant. For alternatives with a price, platform or date constraint, or to search by need, use search_products.

input.name: limit
input.description: How many products to return (default 10).

input.name: product
input.description: Slug, name or Product Hunt URL of the product to find alternatives for, e.g. notion or cursor.

items.name: get_categories
items.description: List all available Product Hunt categories with their slugs. - When to use: When you need to find the right slug for search_products' category filter, or when the user asks what categories Product Hunt has, or wants to browse available topics. - Returns: All searchable categories organised by parent/child hierarchy with slugs. Use the slug values directly as search_products(category).

items.name: get_launch
items.description: Read one launch you own or manage as its hunter, maker or product team member: its content, what still needs work, and what can still change. In the result: - status is draft, unscheduled, scheduled or live. Until its launch day starts only you and its makers can see it; once live, every change is public. - assessment lists what still needs a change or a decision, the programs (contests, Hypership) open on its launch day, and investor questions with their prompt IDs. Resolution options are alternatives; suggestions are optional. - editable_fields names the fields that can still change. You are

input.name: launch_id
input.description: Numeric ID of a submitted launch or UUID of an unsubmitted draft, from list_my_launches or a launch tool.

items.name: get_launch_context
items.description: Read composer limits, account eligibility, midnight-Pacific date availability, the existing product a link belongs to, your matching draft, and bounded topic/category/maker/funding backer/shoutout product suggestions. With no product, the launch is a new product and needs no product question. Availability is a snapshot, not a reservation.

input.name: category
input.description: Category name to search; returns category IDs for categories.

input.name: funding_backer
input.description: Funding backer name to search; returns backer IDs for fundingBackers.

input.name: launch_date
input.description: YYYY-MM-DD day in America/Los_Angeles to check for a launch at 00:00 Pacific; the result is in date.

input.name: maker
input.description: Username or name to search; returns user IDs for makerIds.

input.name: product_id
input.description: Numeric Product ID; resolves this product instead of url's.

input.name: shoutout_product
input.description: Product name to search; returns product IDs for shoutouts productId.

input.name: topic
input.description: Topic name to search; returns topic IDs for topics.

input.name: url
input.description: Product link to resolve: its existing product, your unsubmitted draft for this exact link, and a recent launch of it.

items.name: get_my_account
items.description: Return the authenticated Product Hunt account identity.

items.name: get_product_leaderboard
items.description: Get Product Hunt's official leaderboard: the products that ranked for a day, in rank order, each with its ranked launch and points. date is a day (YYYY-MM-DD); it also takes an ISO week (YYYY-Www), a month (YYYY-MM) or a year (YYYY). Omit date for today. Days are Pacific time, and today's leaderboard is still changing. To search or filter launches, use search_products.

input.name: cursor
input.description: The next_cursor from a previous response, sent with the same date. Paging covers at most 100 products.

input.name: date
input.description: A day (YYYY-MM-DD), ISO week (YYYY-Www), month (YYYY-MM) or year (YYYY), Pacific time. Omit for today.

input.name: limit
input.description: How many products to return (default 10).

items.name: get_product_profile
items.description: Get detailed information about a product including description, makers, categories, social links, pricing, ratings, review highlights, a company object (YC batch, founded date, team size, operating status), a funding object (total raised, latest round, notable investors), and series_a_band when the latest launch ranks in the top bands of Product Hunt's Series A forecast. - When to use: "tell me about [product]", "what is [product]?", "who made [product]?", "give me info on [product]", or wants a comprehensive overview of a specific product. - Args: product_name (product name, slug, or the name

input.name: product_name
input.description: Product name or slug to look up (e.g., "notion", "linear", "figma").

items.name: list_my_launches
items.description: List launches you own or manage as hunter, maker, or active product team member, most recently changed first. status is draft (not submitted), unscheduled, scheduled, or live. Read one with get_launch and its launch_id. permitted_actions lists the tools and website editing that apply to each item; the write tools appear only when this connection can edit launches.

input.name: cursor
input.description: next_cursor from the previous page; valid only with the same product_id, status and limit.

input.name: limit
input.description: Items per page; defaults to 20.

input.name: product_id
input.description: Numeric Product ID; only launches for this product.

input.name: status
input.description: Only launches with this status.

items.name: prepare_launch_asset
items.description: Stage a thumbnail or gallery image for a launch you own or manage. Staging changes neither the displayed images nor the launch revision: once the asset is ready, attach it with update_launch thumbnailAssetId or ordered galleryAssetIds for the same launch_id. Images are PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, up to 10 MB, 10000 pixels per side and 40 megapixels. Send the bytes one of three ways: 1. source_url, when the image is already at a public URL. 2. For a local file, prefer the upload: call without source_url or content, then POST the file as multipart field file to upload.url on www.producthunt.com with

input.name: content
input.description: Base64 image bytes from a tool such as base64, at most 3 MB decoded, without a data: prefix; line breaks are ignored. Not with source_url. Your client may allow less than 3 MB; if it rejects the call, send a smaller image.

input.name: idempotency_key
input.description: Names this asset for this account and connection; reuse it only with the same launch_id, kind and source_url. Retry with the same key to get the same asset, a fresh ticket, or another try at content after a failure; a ready asset accepts only its same bytes.

input.name: kind
input.description: thumbnail assets go in thumbnailAssetId, gallery assets in galleryAssetIds.

input.name: launch_id
input.description: Numeric ID of a submitted launch or UUID of an unsubmitted draft, from list_my_launches or a launch tool.

input.name: source_url
input.description: Public HTTP or HTTPS image URL the server downloads. Not with content.

items.name: search_products
items.description: Search Product Hunt products by name, what they do, or launch date. Each result is a product with up to 3 launches nested, matched first. Use it to look up a product by name, find tools for a need, find products with an MCP server, or browse by category and date. For a leaderboard use get_product_leaderboard; for alternatives to one product use get_alternatives; for reviews and full details use get_product_profile. Omit filters and sort the user did not ask for. Put constraints in their own fields, not in query. Examples: - "is Raindrop on Product Hunt?" → {"query": "raindrop"} - "free open so

input.name: category
input.description: Only products in this category: a slug from get_categories.

input.name: cursor
input.description: The next_cursor from a previous response, sent with the same other arguments. Paging covers at most 100 results.

input.name: has_mcp_server
input.description: true for products that offer an MCP server only; any for no filter.

input.name: launched_after
input.description: Only products with a launch on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD, Pacific time. For named periods.

input.name: launched_before
input.description: Only products with a launch on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD, Pacific time. For named periods.

input.name: launched_within_days
input.description: Only products with a launch in the last N days (1 = today). Do not combine with launched_after or launched_before.

input.name: limit
input.description: How many products to return (default 10).

input.name: open_source
input.description: true for open source products only; any for no filter.

input.name: platform
input.description: Only products available on this platform; any for no filter. From the app store links on the product. Mac, Windows and other platforms are not covered: put them in query.

input.name: pricing
input.description: Only products with this pricing; any for no pricing filter.

input.name: query
input.description: A product name or a short phrase for what it does. Constraints such as price, open source, YC or dates go in their own fields, not here.

input.name: sort
input.description: Leave out unless the user asks for an order; a date window alone does not need one. Default: relevance with query, otherwise highest_rated. newest is the latest launch first; most_points ranks by the points of launches in the window.

input.name: yc
input.description: true for Y Combinator companies only; any for no filter.

items.name: start_launch
items.description: Start a launch for a product link, or resume your existing unsubmitted launch for the same link and product choice without changing it (created: false). Omit product_choice for a new product; nothing needs confirming. Only when get_launch_context finds an existing product for the link, ask the user whether this launch belongs to it, then send product_choice "existing" with its product_id; a link that belongs to an existing product is refused as new. values uses the same fields as update_launch changes, except images, which are prepared for the returned launch_id. The launch starts as a private

input.name: idempotency_key
input.description: Retry key for this account and connection, bound to url, product_choice, product_id and values; reuse it only for an identical retry.

input.name: product_choice
input.description: Defaults to new.

input.name: product_id
input.description: Numeric product ID from get_launch_context product.id; required with product_choice existing and refused otherwise.

input.name: url
input.description: The product link, http or https, without spaces; not a Product Hunt link.

input.name: values
input.description: Initial fields, in update_launch changes names; used only when a new draft is created.

items.name: submit_feedback
items.description: Send feedback about the Product Hunt MCP to the Product Hunt team. Call only when the user explicitly asks you or approves requests to do so. Encourage the user to leave feedback when a tool or upload fails, results are wrong or confusing, a capability is missing, or a step needs a workaround, unless they've previously declined. Never include secrets or personal details about anyone.

input.name: impact
input.description: blocked: the task could not be finished. worked_around: finished another way. friction: finished, but harder than it should be.

input.name: kind
input.description: broken: a tool failed or returned wrong data. confusing: a tool, its arguments, or its output were unclear. missing: no tool offers what the user needed. idea: a suggestion to improve an existing tool.

input.name: message
input.description: What the user wanted, what you tried (tool calls and arguments), what happened, and what would have helped.

input.name: tool
input.description: Name of the tool the feedback is about, if any.

items.name: submit_launch
items.description: Submit a draft launch so it is scheduled for its launch day, or created unscheduled and not public when it has no launchDate. It always takes two calls, and only the second one submits. 1. Call without confirmation_token. Nothing is submitted; the result is outcome needs_confirmation with preview.submit (the complete submission as Product Hunt would carry it out), side_effects (what it does and what becomes public), warnings and a confirmation_token valid for 15 minutes. validation_failed means something blocks submission; fix it with update_launch first. 2. Show the user the preview and side_

input.name: confirmation_token
input.description: confirmation_token from the needs_confirmation result; send it only after the user approved that preview. Empty means omitted.

input.name: idempotency_key
input.description: Retry key for this account and connection, bound to launch_id and confirmation_token. If the outcome is unknown, retry the identical request with the same key; a retry returns the launch, even after the token expires.

input.name: launch_id
input.description: UUID launch_id of the draft to submit, from list_my_launches or a launch tool.

input.name: preview
input.description: True only previews, as omitting confirmation_token does. Cannot be combined with confirmation_token.

items.name: update_launch
items.description: Change a launch you own or manage, at any status. Change only fields in get_launch editable_fields. - Draft: a draft is private, so every change, including added makers, applies directly (outcome applied), even when incomplete. It never submits, schedules or enrolls the launch. - Submitted or live: public changes, moving the launch's day, and notifying added makers return outcome needs_confirmation and change nothing. Which edits are public cannot be predicted, since even a launch that is not live yet can change a public product page, so send changes without preview and let the server decide.

input.name: changes
input.description: Fields from get_launch values. Omit to keep; null clears; lists and investorConnectionResponses replace the whole value. Required values cannot be cleared (validation_failed).

input.name: confirmation_token
input.description: Valid for 15 minutes. After user approval, resend the same launch, revision and changes with this token, without preview. Bound to this account and connection; differences are confirmation_invalid. Empty means omitted.

input.name: expected_revision
input.description: Revision from get_launch or the previous result.

input.name: idempotency_key
input.description: If the outcome is unknown, retry the identical request with this same key to avoid applying it twice.

input.name: launch_id
input.description: Numeric ID of a submitted launch or UUID of an unsubmitted draft, from list_my_launches or a launch tool.

input.name: preview
input.description: True changes nothing and returns needs_confirmation with a preview and token, even for private edits. Cannot be combined with confirmation_token.

items.name: launch-preview
items.title: Launch Preview
items.description: How a launch page looks with the previewed submission or edit

items.name: get_company
items.description: Returns one production company by slug, id, or productionlist.com/production-contact/… URL, with its description, categories, website, url, and the productions attached to it (active first). Contact details are never included.

items.name: get_production
items.description: Returns one production by slug, id, or productionlist.com/production/… URL: synopsis, stage, dates, locations, attached companies, and attached people with their roles (producer, casting director, director, writer…). Contact details are never included; the contacts field states whether contacts are on file for members.

input.name: id_or_slug
input.description: Slug (preferred), numeric id, or the page URL

items.name: get_taxonomies
items.description: Returns the valid slugs for the stage, type, status and company category filters.

items.name: search_companies
items.description: Finds production companies by name substring (q) or company category slug. Returns name, categories, description, website and url; a company's productions are not included.

items.name: search_productions
items.description: Searches and filters film and TV productions. q matches the title only (not companies or people). stage: in-development | in-pre-production | in-production | in-post-production | completed. city / state / country match the shooting location (state is a two-letter US or Canadian code such as GA; UK regions by name, such as England). since = first detected on or after an ISO date; updated_since = changed on or after. Results are newest first. Each result includes its public page url, updated_at, and production_dates.start where known.

input.name: limit
input.description: Results per page (free tier caps at 20)

input.name: q
input.description: Title substring, case-insensitive

input.name: since
input.description: ISO date: only productions first detected on or after

input.name: state
input.description: Two-letter US state / Canadian province, or a UK region name

input.name: status
input.description: Detection status slug, e.g. casting

input.name: type
input.description: Production type slug, e.g. feature-film or series

input.name: updated_since
input.description: ISO date: only productions updated on or after

items.name: prowler_cloud_apply_organization_discovery
items.description: Apply a succeeded discovery: create/link Prowler providers for the selected accounts, subscriptions or projects and build the OU/management-group/folder hierarchy. For AWS organizations, pass the `accounts` to onboard. Onboarding the ENTIRE organization (every discovered account) requires `all_accounts=true`, so confirm that with the user first. For Azure, `subscriptions` is required and must be non-empty; for GCP, `projects` is required and must be non-empty. items.name: check_message
items.description: Check a suspicious email, SMS, WhatsApp message, link or screenshot for scam signals. Controleer een verdachte mail, sms, WhatsApp-bericht, link of screenshot op signalen van oplichting. Documentation: [REDACTED URI]

items.name: Scamchecker resultaat
items.description: Visuele uitslag van een nagekeken bericht

items.name: count_smql_queries
items.description: Count the public scans matching each of up to 25 SMQL queries in one request, for example to see which indicators of a campaign are selective. Each count stops at 10,000 (exact_count is then false); a count that ran out of time has count_unavailable true, and a query that does not parse gets its own error without failing the others. With sites true, queries with 10 or more matches also get the number of distinct sites, how many of them are rated high risk, and whether the value is shared widely by unrelated sites. Counts are cached for up to 30 minutes.

input.name: queries
input.description: SMQL queries to count, 1 to 25, each up to 2000 characters.

input.name: sites
input.description: Also summarise the sites behind each query with 10 or more matches: distinct sites, how many are rated high risk, and whether the value is shared widely by unrelated sites.

items.name: find_js_fingerprint_similar_by_hash
items.description: Find JavaScript files similar to the file with this content SHA-256, above threshold (default 0.7), up to limit results; exclude_exact_matches drops identical copies. Useful for finding modified versions of a known script.

input.name: content_sha256
input.description: SHA-256 of a JavaScript file's content (64 hex characters).

input.name: exclude_exact_matches
input.description: Leave out files whose content is identical.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, 1 to 100.

input.name: threshold
input.description: Minimum similarity, 0 to 1 (default 0.7).

items.name: get_ai_analysis
items.description: Get the AI analysis of one scan: classification (LEGITIMATE to CONFIRMED_SCAM), scam type, risk score, confidence, impersonated brand and the key evidence behind it. The analysis is produced a few minutes after the scan completes and returns not found until then. It can disagree with the scanner's own security verdict. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_analyzer_results
items.description: List which analysis modules ran for one scan (for example JavaScript fingerprinting and AI analysis), with each module's status, success flag and timing. Useful for checking why a result is missing. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_analyzer_stats
items.description: Get platform-wide statistics for the scan analysis modules: the modules and their run counts. Describes the service, not a particular scan.

items.name: get_api_root
items.description: Get the ScanMalware API's name, version, status, main endpoints and feature list.

items.name: get_bot_protection
items.description: Get the bot-protection and CAPTCHA services detected on a scanned page (for example Cloudflare Turnstile), with a detected flag. Phishing kits often use these to hide from scanners. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_capabilities_by_date
items.description: Get the size of ScanMalware's detection content (indicators, detection rules, ClamAV signatures) on a given date (scan_date, YYYY-MM-DD).

input.name: scan_date
input.description: Date to report, as YYYY-MM-DD.

items.name: get_clipboard_events
items.description: Get the clipboard writes the page attempted while it was scanned, with the event count and whether collection ran. Empty with an explanatory note when the page wrote nothing. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_clipboard_stats
items.description: Get clipboard and pastejacking statistics across the archive: event totals, detections and daily activity.

items.name: get_cpe_by_scan
items.description: List the CPE identifiers (product and version names in the NVD format) derived from the technologies detected on a scanned page, with their source. Useful for matching against vulnerability data. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_cpe_stats
items.description: Get CPE statistics across the archive: scans with CPEs, unique CPEs, total detections, top vendors and products.

items.name: get_ct_certificates
items.description: Get the certificates issued for a domain according to Certificate Transparency logs, with a found flag.

input.name: domain
input.description: Domain name, for example example.com.

items.name: get_ct_dns_records
items.description: List subdomains of a domain found through Certificate Transparency, with their DNS records (type, IP addresses, TTL) and when they were seen. Useful for finding the other hosts of a domain.

input.name: domain
input.description: Domain name, for example example.com.

items.name: get_ct_domains_by_ip
items.description: List domains that Certificate Transparency and DNS data associate with an IP address, with record counts and the total.

input.name: ip_address
input.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address to look up.

items.name: get_ct_root_domains_by_ip
items.description: List the registrable domains that resolved to an IP address when their TLS certificates were issued, alphabetical, each with the hostnames seen under it, the number of resolution records and when they were first and last seen. A domain that moved to the address after its certificate was issued is not listed. window is recent, standard (default) or extended; paginated by limit (1 to 500) and next_cursor. Can be briefly unavailable under load (HTTP 503); retry after a pause.

input.name: cursor
input.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit for the first page.

input.name: ip_address
input.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address the domains resolved to.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, 1 to 500.

input.name: window
input.description: How far back to list: recent, standard (default) or extended.

items.name: get_ct_similar_domains
items.description: Find domains with names similar to a domain in Certificate Transparency data (for example lookalikes and typosquats), each with a certificate count and the kind of similarity.

input.name: domain
input.description: Domain name, for example example.com.

items.name: get_ct_timeline
items.description: Get the certificate history of a domain from Certificate Transparency: when certificates were issued and when the certificate changed.

input.name: domain
input.description: Domain name, for example example.com.

items.name: get_dns_history
items.description: Get every DNS answer a name has given, newest first: the records seen when public pages using it were scanned and the addresses it resolved to when TLS certificates for it were published, each with first and last seen. For a domain this includes its _dmarc record and a wildcard probe; for an IP address, its reverse-DNS (PTR) names. DNS lookups during scans started on 28 October 2026. name is a hostname, domain or IP address; limit is 1 to 500.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, 1 to 500.

input.name: name
input.description: Hostname, domain or IP address whose DNS answers to list, for example login.example.com.

items.name: get_domain_history
items.description: Get the scan history of a domain with the total count and the scans, paginated with page and limit.

input.name: domain
input.description: Domain name such as example.com, or an IP address.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, 1 to 100.

input.name: page
input.description: Page number, starting at 1.

items.name: get_domain_hosts
items.description: List every host seen for a domain (or IP address) across its newest scans, grouped by evidence: observed (the browser requested it) and scripts (a script the browser loaded) by default; declared (named in Content-Security-Policy, intent only), static (a URL in script source) and referenced (only a string or comment) on request in sources. subdomains_only keeps hosts below the domain. max_scans (1 to 1000, default 200) is how many scans to aggregate; limit (1 to 10000, default 500) caps hosts per source.

input.name: domain
input.description: Domain name such as example.com, or an IP address.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum hosts per evidence kind, 1 to 10000 (default 500).

input.name: max_scans
input.description: How many of the domain's newest scans to aggregate, 1 to 1000 (default 200).

input.name: sources
input.description: Evidence kinds to include: observed and scripts by default; add declared (Content-Security-Policy), static (URLs in script source) or referenced (strings and comments only).

input.name: subdomains_only
input.description: Return only hosts strictly below the domain.

items.name: get_domain_scans
items.description: List the recent scans of a domain and its subdomains, newest first, up to limit; status filters by scan status. Each row has matched_on: 'url' when the scan was submitted for a host under this domain, and only 'final_url' when another site redirected there. A verdict on a final_url-only row belongs to the submitted host, not to this domain.

input.name: domain
input.description: Domain name such as example.com, or an IP address.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, 1 to 100.

input.name: status
input.description: Only scans with this status: queued, processing, completed or failed; omit for all.

items.name: get_domain_stats
items.description: Get scan counts for a domain: total, unique, completed and failed scans, first and latest scan, and scans in the last 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days.

input.name: domain
input.description: Domain name such as example.com, or an IP address.

items.name: get_favicon
items.description: Get the favicon recorded for a scan_id: the original icon's MD5 and mmh3 hashes, the ones favicon search indexes, and the stored copy's size, SHA-256 and image, base64-encoded. found is false when no favicon is stored for the scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_favicon_stats
items.description: Get favicon statistics across the archive: total favicons, those seen in the last 24 hours and the most common hashes with sample URLs. This aggregate query can take up to 90 seconds by default.

items.name: get_file_analysis
items.description: Get what reading one file delivered by a public scan found (a download, a file link, a command put on the clipboard, or a file inside one of those): type, size and hashes, verdict and its reasons, files inside it, Windows program details (signer, version information, compiler, build time, imports, debug file), capabilities with ATT&CK techniques, matching rules, antivirus detection names, embedded URLs and identifiers that tie it to other files. sha256 is the file's SHA-256 (64 hex characters).

input.name: sha256
input.description: SHA-256 of the file (64 hex characters).

items.name: get_health
items.description: Check whether the ScanMalware API is up. Returns the service status.

items.name: get_ids_alerts
items.description: Get intrusion detection (IDS) alerts raised on the network traffic recorded during one scan, with a severity breakdown and total count. Empty when no rule fired. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_ip_stats
items.description: Get statistics for an IP address across the archive: total scans, unique URLs, first and last seen, geolocation, ASN and organisation, BGP and DNS data; paginated.

input.name: ip_address
input.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address to report on.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, 1 to 100.

input.name: page
input.description: Page number, starting at 1.

items.name: get_jarm_signatures
items.description: Get the JARM TLS server fingerprints measured for the hosts in one scan, with whether each matches a known signature. A shared JARM often points to the same server software or hosting platform, so it is a weak pivot on its own. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_jarm_stats
items.description: Get JARM statistics across the archive, including the most common signatures. Common signatures usually belong to large hosting platforms.

items.name: get_js_fingerprints
items.description: List the JavaScript files a scanned page loaded, each with its fingerprint: hashes (SHA-256, SHA-1, MD5, normalized and fuzzy), size metrics, detected library and bundler. The include_* options add function lists, HTTP headers or ML vector details. Paginated with limit (default 20) and offset: total_scripts is the scan's number of scripts and fingerprints_count the number returned. Useful for collecting script hashes to search for elsewhere. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: include_functions
input.description: Include the list of functions extracted from each script.

input.name: include_http_headers
input.description: Include the HTTP response headers each script was served with.

input.name: include_vectors_info
input.description: Include whether machine-learning similarity vectors exist for each script.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of scripts, 1 to 100 (default 20).

input.name: offset
input.description: Number of results to skip, for paging; 0 starts at the first result.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_js_library_inventory
items.description: List the JavaScript libraries and versions detected across the archive, with how many scans used each; library filters to one library and min_count drops rare versions. Identifiers are lowercase names such as 'react', 'jquery' or 'nextjs'.

input.name: library
input.description: Only this library, for example jquery.

input.name: min_count
input.description: Leave out libraries with fewer fingerprints than this.

items.name: get_js_runtime_behaviour
items.description: Get the runtime JavaScript behaviour recorded for one scan: overall risk, risk scores, number of scripts, eval and Function-constructor calls and high-risk events, with a behavioural signature and composite hash. include_detailed_events adds the individual events. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: include_detailed_events
input.description: Include every recorded event; this can be very large (10 MB or more).

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_js_runtime_coverage
items.description: Get how many scans have runtime JavaScript fingerprints: coverage percentage and the number of unique composite hashes and signatures. Describes the service, not a scan.

items.name: get_js_runtime_health
items.description: Check whether the runtime JavaScript analysis service is up, with its version.

items.name: get_js_runtime_stats
items.description: Get platform-wide statistics for runtime JavaScript analysis: risk distribution, averages and totals of eval calls and high-risk events. Describes the service, not a scan.

items.name: get_js_segments_by_scan
items.description: List the code segments (functions and blocks) extracted from one scan's JavaScript, each with location, length, snippet and hashes; script_url narrows to one file, paginated with limit and offset. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, 1 to 100; omit for the API's default.

input.name: offset
input.description: Number of results to skip, for paging; 0 starts at the first result.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

input.name: script_url
input.description: Only segments from this script URL.

items.name: get_js_segments_suspicious
items.description: List the JavaScript code segments from one scan scored as suspicious, above min_risk_score, with location, snippet and risk details; paginated with limit and offset. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, 1 to 100; omit for the API's default.

input.name: min_risk_score
input.description: Minimum risk score, 0 to 100.

input.name: offset
input.description: Number of results to skip, for paging; 0 starts at the first result.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_js_segments_unknown
items.description: List the JavaScript code segments from one scan that match no known library, at least min_code_length long; these are usually the page's own or a kit's code. Paginated with limit and offset. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, 1 to 100; omit for the API's default.

input.name: min_code_length
input.description: Minimum segment length in characters.

input.name: offset
input.description: Number of results to skip, for paging; 0 starts at the first result.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_jsfingerprint
items.description: Get one JavaScript fingerprint record by its numeric fingerprint_id: the script URL, scan, hashes, metrics and ML vector information; include_functions and include_http_headers add more detail.

input.name: fingerprint_id
input.description: Numeric ID of a JavaScript fingerprint, as listed among a scan's scripts.

input.name: include_functions
input.description: Include the list of functions extracted from each script.

input.name: include_http_headers
input.description: Include the HTTP response headers each script was served with.

items.name: get_jsfingerprint_bundle_stats
items.description: Get statistics on bundled JavaScript across the archive for a date range: share of bundled files and the breakdown by bundler (webpack, vite, rollup and so on) and module format.

input.name: from_date
input.description: Start of the date range, ISO 8601 (for example 2026-11-01); omit for the API's default.

input.name: to_date
input.description: End of the date range, ISO 8601 (for example 2026-11-12); omit for the API's default.

items.name: get_jsfingerprint_hash_prevalence
items.description: For each script in one scan, report how common its hash is across the archive, which separates widely used library files from rare, page-specific code. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_jsfingerprint_library_stats
items.description: Get statistics on JavaScript library detection across the archive for a date range: total fingerprints, detection rate and the most common libraries, each with its most common versions. limit (default 100) caps the libraries and versions_limit (default 10) the versions listed per library; total_libraries and each library's version_count give the full numbers.

input.name: from_date
input.description: Start of the date range, ISO 8601 (for example 2026-11-01); omit for the API's default.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of libraries, 1 to 1000 (default 100).

input.name: min_count
input.description: Leave out libraries seen fewer times than this.

input.name: to_date
input.description: End of the date range, ISO 8601 (for example 2026-11-12); omit for the API's default.

input.name: versions_limit
input.description: Maximum number of versions listed per library, 0 to 1000 (default 10).

items.name: get_jsfingerprint_similar
items.description: Find JavaScript files whose fingerprint is similar to the one with this fingerprint_id, above threshold (0 to 1), paginated with limit and offset. exclude_same_scan drops matches from the same scan. Useful for finding variants of one script.

input.name: exclude_same_scan
input.description: Leave out files from the same scan.

input.name: fingerprint_id
input.description: Numeric ID of a JavaScript fingerprint, as listed among a scan's scripts.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, 1 to 100.

input.name: offset
input.description: Number of results to skip, for paging; 0 starts at the first result.

input.name: threshold
input.description: Minimum similarity, 0 to 1.

items.name: get_jsfingerprint_similarity_counts
items.description: Count how many archived JavaScript files are similar to the one with this fingerprint_id, per similarity model (composite, CodeBERT, GraphCodeBERT, AST and handcrafted features), capped at max_count. This query can take up to 90 seconds by default.

input.name: fingerprint_id
input.description: Numeric ID of a JavaScript fingerprint, as listed among a scan's scripts.

input.name: max_count
input.description: Stop counting at this number per model.

input.name: threshold
input.description: Minimum similarity, 0 to 1.

items.name: get_jsfingerprint_source
items.description: Get the stored source code of one JavaScript file by its numeric fingerprint_id, with its SHA-256, URL and length. Source can be long.

input.name: fingerprint_id
input.description: Numeric ID of a JavaScript fingerprint, as listed among a scan's scripts.

items.name: get_latest_capabilities
items.description: Get the current size of ScanMalware's detection content: indicator count, malware detection rules and ClamAV signatures.

items.name: get_malware_by_scan
items.description: Get the malware detections for files the scanned page delivered, with threat names, detection counts and the detection source. Empty when nothing was detected. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_malware_stats
items.description: Get malware detection statistics across the archive: overall and last-24-hour counts, top threats and hourly trend.

items.name: get_netlog
items.description: Describe the network log (Chrome NetLog) for a scan_id: whether one exists, its size, and its encoding. The log itself is not returned - these are routinely tens of megabytes gzipped.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_ocr_by_scan
items.description: Get the text read by OCR from the scan's screenshot, with language, confidence, word and character counts and any regions flagged as suspicious. Useful when page text is drawn as images. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_ocr_stats
items.description: Get OCR statistics across the archive: scans with OCR text, average confidence and length, language distribution and daily counts.

items.name: get_open_graph
items.description: Get the Open Graph and Twitter card metadata the scanned page declared (title, description, image, site name). Phishing pages often copy a brand's metadata. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_pastejacking
items.description: Get pastejacking findings for one scan: attempts by the page to replace what a visitor copies, a common trick for making victims paste malicious commands. Includes a detected flag and a note. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_pcap_metadata
items.description: Describe the packet capture (PCAP) recorded during one scan: whether it exists, its size, compression and content type. The capture itself is not returned. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_platform_stats
items.description: Get the current scan queue length, running scans and scans completed in the last 24 hours by visibility.

items.name: get_popular_technologies
items.description: List the most frequently detected web technologies over the last days (paginated).

input.name: days
input.description: How many days to look back; omit for the API's default.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, 1 to 100.

input.name: page
input.description: Page number, starting at 1.

items.name: get_rdap
items.description: Get registration data (RDAP) for the scanned domain and its IP addresses: registrar, registration and expiry dates, domain age, nameservers and status. A very young domain is a common phishing signal. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_recent_scans
items.description: List the most recent public scans, newest first (paginated with page and limit). Each row has the scan ID, URL, status, visibility and submission time. Unlisted and private scans are never included.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, 1 to 100.

input.name: page
input.description: Page number, starting at 1.

items.name: get_recent_threats
items.description: List malware threats detected in scans during the last hours (default window set by the API), with totals and grouping by threat.

input.name: hours
input.description: How many hours to look back; omit for the API's default window.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, 1 to 100.

items.name: get_recent_yara_threats
items.description: List YARA rule matches from scans in the last hours (1 to 168, default 24), each with the scan, URL, rule, category, severity and confidence.

input.name: hours
input.description: How many hours to look back, 1 to 168 (default 24).

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum number of results, 1 to 100.

items.name: get_safe_browsing
items.description: Get Google Safe Browsing threats found for the URLs in one scan, with a has_threats flag. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: get_safe_browsing_stats
items.description: Get Google Safe Browsing statistics across the archive: total threats, threats in the last 7 days, scans with threats and threat types.

items.name: get_scan_deobfuscation
items.description: List every script one scan captured, once per distinct content: whether and how it was obfuscated (tool and level), whether decoding or unpacking worked, and what became visible only after decoding (hosts, URLs, wallet addresses, threat-feed matches, messaging channels, WebAssembly). Each entry has the fingerprint_id of its full analysis. The level says how much effort went into hiding the code, not whether it is dangerous. scan_id is the UUID of a ScanMalware scan.

input.name: scan_id
input.description: UUID of a ScanMalware scan: the scan_id of a submission or of a search result.

items.name: certificate_pem
items.description: TLS certificate PEM for a scan_id.

items.name: pcap_capture
items.description: Gzip-compressed PCAP capture (.pcap.gz) for a scan_id; gunzip it before opening it in a pcap reader.

items.name: rss_feed
items.description: RSS feed of recent scans.

items.name: screenshot_png
items.description: PNG screenshot for a scan_id.

items.name: get_build_guide
items.description: A published build guide by slug as markdown: parts, assembly steps, connections and firmware.

input.name: slug
input.description: The guide's slug as returned by search_build_guides, e.g. 'build-a-co2-room-monitor'.

items.name: get_part
items.description: One part from the catalogue by slug, as JSON: name, brand, part number, description, category, an available vendor price (lowest offer in one currency, USD when available, e.g. 'from 4.5 USD'), pinout and a link to its Schematik page. Brand, part number, description, price and pinout can be null when unavailable.

input.name: slug
input.description: The part's slug as returned by search_parts, e.g. 'bme280-i2c-sensor'.

items.name: search_build_guides
items.description: Search published Schematik build guides: complete projects with parts, wiring and firmware. Leave query empty to list featured guides first. Returns a JSON list of guides with a link and a remixUrl; pass a result's slug to get_build_guide for the full guide.

input.name: board
input.description: Only return guides for this board. Omit for all boards.

input.name: limit
input.description: How many guides to return at most. Fewer come back when fewer guides match.

input.name: query
input.description: What the project should do or use, matched against guide titles, descriptions and boards, e.g. 'weather station'. Leave empty to browse guides, featured ones first.

items.name: search_parts
items.description: Search Schematik's public electronics parts catalogue (boards, sensors, displays, modules) by name, brand, part number or use. Returns a JSON list of parts, best matches first; pass a result's slug to get_part for its pinout and price.

input.name: limit
input.description: How many parts to return at most. Fewer come back when fewer parts match.

input.name: query
input.description: Words to match, e.g. a part name, brand, part number or use such as 'BME280' or 'oled display'. Parts matching any word are returned, best matches first.

items.name: append_explainer_chunk

items.name: snomed_expand
items.description: Expand a SNOMED CT value set using FHIR ValueSet/$expand. The primary tool for retrieving concept sets via ECL (Expression Constraint Language) queries. Works on Snowstorm and Lite when FHIR is available. WHEN TO USE: retrieving concepts matching an ECL expression (most common use case), getting members of a reference set, counting concepts in a subhierarchy (use summary_only=true), text-filtering within a concept set, or retrieving attribute values across a concept set (dotted notation). VALUE SET URL FORMAT: Subtype query: [REDACTED URI]<<CONCEPTID Attribute query: http:

items.name: snomed_get_ancestors
items.description: Get ancestor concepts of a SNOMED concept (parents, grandparents, etc. via IS-A hierarchy). Traverses upward through IS-A to find the classification position of a concept. Set direct_only=true to return only immediate parents. Optionally specify terminology and/or target; defaults to the server's default terminology.

items.name: snomed_get_children
items.description: Get direct IS-A children of a SNOMED concept (one level down in the hierarchy). More efficient than ECL for simple hierarchy browsing when you only need immediate children. WHEN TO USE: exploring the shape of a subhierarchy before writing an ECL query, understanding how a concept is subdivided at the next level, or lightweight hierarchy browsing without full ECL overhead. NOT FOR: transitive closure (all descendants) — use snomed_expand with <<CONCEPTID. Not for attribute-based queries — use snomed_expand with ECL. Not for filtering by description or metadata — use snomed_expand with filters.

items.name: snomed_get_descendants
items.description: Get all descendant concepts of a SNOMED concept (children, grandchildren, etc. via IS-A hierarchy). Transitive closure downward, equivalent to <<X in ECL but returned as a hierarchy structure. Use snomed_expand with ECL if you need a flat concept list with attribute constraints instead. Use count and offset to paginate large result sets. Optionally specify terminology and/or target; defaults to the server's default terminology.

items.name: snomed_lookup
items.description: Retrieve full concept details via FHIR CodeSystem/$lookup for a known SNOMED CT concept ID. Returns the FSN, synonyms, parent concepts, and all defining attributes with their values. WHEN TO USE: verifying a concept ID before using it in an ECL expression, inspecting the full attribute modelling of a specific concept, retrieving all synonyms and descriptions for a concept, checking whether a concept is active or inactive, or confirming the correct concept ID for a common attribute (e.g. finding site). If the code does not exist, returns found=false with a message (not an error). NOT FOR: searc

items.name: snomed_validate_code

WHEN TO USE: confirming a concept ID is valid and active before storing or querying, checking whether a concept has been inactivated (retired/replaced), handling legacy codes from EHR data (check status before using in ECL), or verifying a code belongs to a specific edition or version. Preferred approach when history supplements are unavailable (they are NOT supported on this server). Use this to check individual inactive codes

items.name: list_artists

Other rows format badges as Name (new) — active contest: …. Do not nest extra parentheses. Examples: On your own — your style, no cowriting artist; Graham Colton (new); Finesse2tymes — active contest: Finesse is looking for song ideas for his next album.

Use when the user asks what songs they made, after generation completes if the player did not appear, when complimentary generations are used up, or when they say songs are missing from My Tracks. input.name: limit

items.name: list_top_tracks

Payback is calculated only when an implementation cost is supplied. Returns weekly and annual hours reclaimed, annual capacity value, payback months, the assumptions used and a recommended next step. Results are planning estimates, not guaranteed savings or financial advice.

Returns each workflow's score, recommendation, human-review flag and rationale, plus a recommended first workflow and guardrails. It does not connect to or change any system.

input.name: phase

input.name: temp

items.name: ask_cv
items.description: Ask about a Speak2MyCV professional's skills, career history, certifications, education or projects using retrieved CV and profile information. Requires their handle. Missing evidence is reported. Does not contact the person. For profile photos, use get_profile for the same handle; this tool does not return a photo.

input.name: question
input.description: A natural-language question about the person's career.

input.name: slug
input.description: The person's Speak2MyCV handle, e.g. 'itssubhendu' (from <slug>.speak2mycv.com).

items.name: get_profile
items.description: For profile photos, call get_profile and use only its photo URL; never search the web for a picture of the person or substitute a name-matched person card. If no photo is returned, say it is unavailable. Return a Speak2MyCV professional's structured profile (name, title, photo, summary, skills, experience, certifications, education) by slug, taken from their real CV. Use to pull facts without asking a full question.

input.name: slug
input.description: The person's Speak2MyCV handle, e.g. 'itssubhendu' (from <slug>.speak2mycv.com).

items.name: get_profile_fields
items.description: For profile photos, call get_profile and use only its photo URL; never search the web for a picture of the person or substitute a name-matched person card. If no photo is returned, say it is unavailable. Return a Speak2MyCV professional's confirmed fields (skills, experience, education, certifications, links) as typed structuredContent. Same data as get_profile, for agents that read fields programmatically.

input.name: slug
input.description: The person's Speak2MyCV handle, e.g. 'itssubhendu' (from <slug>.speak2mycv.com).

items.name: ping
items.description: Health check. Returns "pong" to confirm the Speak2MyMCP server is reachable.

input.name: message
input.description: Optional text to echo back

items.name: submit_lead
items.description: Preview or send an enquiry to a Speak2MyCV professional from the signed-in user. First call without confirmation_token: no message is sent. Show the returned recipient, sender name/email, exact message and forwarding disclosure, then obtain explicit user confirmation. After confirmation, repeat the same inputs with the returned confirmation_token. The verified sender name/email and message are stored and queued for email and any configured recipient webhook. Sending cannot be recalled. Reusing the same valid receipt does not create another enquiry.

input.name: company
input.description: The user's company, only if they mentioned it.

input.name: confirmation_token
input.description: Receipt from the preview; include only after the user confirms the displayed recipient, sender and message.

input.name: message
input.description: The exact message the user wants to send. Do not include unrelated conversation history.

input.name: slug
input.description: The person's Speak2MyCV handle, e.g. 'itssubhendu' (from <slug>.speak2mycv.com).

items.name: welcome

items.name: compare_sports_apis

Returns a side-by-side table of researched feature support (pregame, live, Bet365, Pinnacle, closing odds, futures, same game parlay, deeplinks, settlement, stats, schedules, WebSocket, MCP server, esports), pricing scale, free tier, sports mentioned in our reviews, the differences between them, and the SportsAPIs.dev review URL for each. Providers must be in the SportsAPIs.dev directory. Do

input.name: providers
input.description: Two to four provider names as developers write them, for example ["The-Odds-API", "OddsPapi", "SportsGamesOdds"].

items.name: find_sports_apis

Filters the providers researched by SportsAPIs.dev by sport, required features (live odds, WebSocket streaming, Bet365 or Pinnacle odds, historical odds, player props, stats, live scores, MCP server), free tier, price tier and region. Returns a ranked short list with a one-line reason and the SportsAPIs.dev review URL for each provider. Ranking: every feature, free tier, price and re

Every value must be carried for a provider to match. Only providers in the SportsAPIs.dev Coverage Map (probed with our own API keys or listed from their docs) can match, so use sport and needs for a general question: [REDACTED URI]

input.name: exclude_providers

input.name: free_tier
input.description: true = only providers with a confirmed free tier or free plan.

input.name: kind
input.description: "odds" for odds and betting-market APIs, "data" for scores, stats and schedules APIs with no odds. Default "any".

input.name: leagues
input.description: Leagues the API must carry odds for, as canonical ids or display names, case-insensitive, for example "NBA", "EPL" or "Premier League". Every value must be carried for a provider to match. Only providers in the SportsAPIs.dev Coverage Map (probed with our own API keys or listed from their docs) can match, so use sport and needs for a general question: [REDACTED URI]

input.name: limit
input.description: How many providers to return. Default 5.

input.name: markets

Every value must be carried for a provider to match. Only providers in the SportsAPIs.dev Coverage Map (probed with our own API keys or listed from their docs) can match, so use sport and needs for a general question: [REDACTED URI]

input.name: max_price_tier

input.description: Sport or league the developer needs, for example "NFL", "soccer", "tennis", "esports", "college football", or "prediction markets" for Kalshi, Polymarket and similar venues. Boosts providers whose review names that sport; it does not exclude the rest.

items.name: get_sports_api_details
items.description: Use this when a developer asks about one specific sports odds or sports data API by name, for example "Is The-Odds-API free?", "Does OddsPapi have a WebSocket?", "OddsJam API pricing", or "Sportradar API review". Returns everything the SportsAPIs.dev review page records: feature support, pricing tiers from our review, free tier, sports mentioned, strengths, the full review text, FAQs, alternatives in the directory, and the review URL. The provider must be in the SportsAPIs.dev directory. Do not use this for a sportsbook, a league, or a betting question.

input.name: provider
input.description: Provider name or slug, for example "OddsPapi", "the odds api", "sportsdata-io".

items.description: Get complete integration guides with code examples and README documentation for integrating Confidence feature flags. integrate Confidence with OpenFeature best practices Returns full integration examples including OpenFeature provider setup, best practices, and configuration for the specified SDK Unlike searchDocumentation which searches general docs, this returns ready-to-use integration code for specific SDKs Use this tool explicitly when the user wants code snippets or integration guides for a particular programming language or SDK.

items.name: searchDocumentation
items.description: Search the Confidence documentation using semantic search to learn about experiments, A/B tests, rollouts, feature flags, metrics, surfaces, insights, and other experiment-related topics. Returns the 10 most relevant chunks from the documentation.

items.name: squarespace_generate_domain_names
items.description: Generate business name ideas from a free-text description. Returns brandable names grouped by tone (neutral, playful, professional, friendly, informative, quirky). Name ideas only: this tool does not check availability or prices. Use this tool first when the user describes a business or idea but has no name or keyword yet, even if they ask for a domain. For example: - "I need a domain for my bakery" - "Find me a .com for the vintage clothing shop I'm opening" - "Help me name my consulting firm" If the user already has a name or keyword ("acmecoffee", "Flour & Fern"), use squarespace_search_dom

input.name: description
input.description: Free-text description of the business or idea, e.g. 'an artisan coffee roaster in Portland'. A full phrase/sentence is expected here.

items.name: squarespace_search_domains
items.description: Search Squarespace's domain catalog for a keyword. Returns matching domains with registration availability, first-year price, renewal price, and checkoutLink on each available domain. Results may include Sponsored domains (suggestionType: sponsored), which receive promotional placement and are often tied to an active promotion or discount. Preserve suggestionType and label these results Sponsored when presenting them; don't present them as purely organic. Use when the user already has a keyword, brand name, or specific domain to look up. Not for WHOIS lookups, DNS or hosting configuration, or

input.name: availableOnly
input.description: Return only available domains (default true). Ignored when checkAvailability=false.

input.description: Whether to check registration availability. Set false for suggestion-only requests to skip availability lookups and respond faster; results will have available=null and checkoutLink=null on every row. Default true.

input.name: limit
input.description: Max results to return (1-50, default 20).

input.name: query
input.description: Short keyword to base suggestions on, e.g. 'acmecoffee', 'acmecoffee.com', or 'nova labs'. Not a sentence.

items.name: check_domain
items.description: Use this prompt to check availability and price for one specific domain name the user has named.

arguments.name: domain
arguments.description: The domain to check, e.g. 'acmecoffee.com' or just 'acmecoffee'.

items.name: find_domain
items.description: Use this prompt to brainstorm and check available domains for a business or idea described by the user.

items.name: purchase_domain
items.description: Context when the user wants to buy, purchase, or register a Squarespace domain. Optional intent describes what the domain should represent.

arguments.name: intent

items.name: add_board_notices
items.description: Use this after analyzing a board to record what looks wrong: contradictions between cards, odd dates (a deadline before the kickoff, a weekend shoot), likely misspellings of names, or missing information. Keep each text short and specific, and pass the IDs of the cards it is about. Do not use it for suggestions or next steps; add those as a note card instead.

input.name: boardId
input.description: Stashiro board ID

items.name: add_page_images
items.description: Use this after list_page_images, once the user has picked which pictures to keep. Adds them as image cards in a grid starting at x, y on a canvas board. Pass width and height from list_page_images so each tile keeps its shape. Paid cloud accounts only.

input.name: boardId
input.description: Destination Stashiro canvas board ID

items.name: add_review_notes
items.description: Use this after reading a board's text to leave editor-style review notes. Each note quotes exact words from one text card (copied character for character), gives a severity (high for errors or contradictions, medium for weak or unclear passages, low for polish) and a short comment. Add a question with 2 to 4 options when the fix depends on the writer's choice. Notes appear beside the card they quote, with Fix it, Answer it and Talk it through in the app.

input.name: boardId
input.description: Stashiro canvas board ID

items.name: arrange_connected_cards
items.description: Arrange 2 to 40 existing linked cards as a mindmap, flow, tree or radial layout using Stashiro's native layout. Preserves sizes and content, avoids other cards, and adjusts link anchors and mind-map branch colors. Include every card to move in cardIds; the selection must form one connected group. Separate stacked cards first. Use connect_cards to add missing links.

items.name: breakdown_script
items.description: Use this when the user shares a screenplay (Fountain, Final Draft XML or plain text) and wants a breakdown, stripboard, shooting schedule or day out of days. Parses scene headings, time of day, speaking parts and page eighths, tags cast, props, wardrobe, vehicles, effects and makeup, then places a scene index table, a breakdown table, tag lists, a stripboard with one coloured strip per scene and the page total per day, a shooting schedule and a day out of days. Reads the first 40,000 characters per call; send longer scripts in parts.

input.name: days
input.description: Shoot days; about five pages a day when omitted

input.name: shotList
input.description: Also add starter shot cards per scene

Internal access checks are combined so empty intermediate pages are never exposed. Continue with the returned cursors until spacesIsDone and boardsIsDone are both true.
