items.name: compare_ai_products
items.description: Compare two to four published catalog products using the same criteria. Distinguishes catalog-record values from verified field evidence and unknowns. Includes stored claim scopes and recorded limitations; no invented scores, winner, pricing, or benchmarks. Use kind and slug returned by discovery.

items.name: discover_ai_products
items.description: Search tasarim.ai's published catalog using concise product names, categories or needs. Category and text matches identify catalog records; verified task filters require stored field evidence. Returns claim scopes, recorded limitations, explicit unknowns and language fallback. Raw unverified descriptions and provider commerce/tracking URLs are withheld. Optional first-party catalog links may carry a fixed visit marker. This bounded catalog does not browse the web or generate media.

items.name: get_ai_product_evidence
items.description: Retrieve stored field claims, source provenance and recorded limitations for one AI product. Catalog profiles are labeled as catalog records, not independent evidence. Provider/evidence commerce/tracking URLs are withheld with reasons. Optional first-party catalog links may carry a fixed visit marker; source dates do not imply live re-verification. Does not expose unpublished drafts or internal review metadata. Use kind and slug returned by discovery.

items.name: check_service_availability
items.description: Check availability, pricing, and scoping questions for a service at the user's location. At the start of a service request, ask for the user's full address (street, city, state and postal code) and say briefly why: it confirms Taskers serve their exact address and pre-fills the booking. If the user is only browsing or would rather not share it, a city + state or a postal code is fine. Pass a street address as streetAddress (the line as the user wrote it, including any unit, e.g. '20 Jay St Apt 3'; don't split it) together with city, state and postalCode. If the response has addressStatus, sett

input.name: addressConfirmed
input.description: Set to true only when calling again after the user confirmed a needs_confirmation suggestedAddress

input.name: city
input.description: City name (e.g., New York, San Francisco)

input.name: postalCode
input.description: US postal code (e.g., 10001)

input.name: service
input.description: The service the user asked for, in their own words (e.g., 'assemble IKEA furniture')

input.name: state
input.description: State/province abbreviation (e.g., NY, CA)

input.name: streetAddress
input.description: Street address line as the user wrote it, including any unit (e.g., '20 Jay St Apt 3'). Requires city, state and postalCode. Don't split it into number, street and unit.

items.name: generate_deep_link
items.description: Create a Taskrabbit job draft and return a deep link into the booking flow. Must be called after check_service_availability so that categoryId, locale, questionnaire, and location are all known; pass location exactly as check_service_availability returned it. If location.precision isn't 'address', first ask the user for their street address (to confirm Taskers serve it and pre-fill the booking) and pass it as streetAddress, city, state and postalCode; if they decline, call with streetAddressDeclined: true. If the response has addressStatus, settle the address as check_service_availability desc

input.name: addressConfirmed
input.description: Set to true only when calling again after the user confirmed a needs_confirmation suggestedAddress

input.name: categoryId
input.description: Category service key (e.g., 'furniture_assembly')

input.name: city
input.description: City of streetAddress

input.name: locale
input.description: BCP 47 locale code (e.g., 'en-US')

input.name: location
input.description: Location returned by check_service_availability, passed back unchanged

input.name: postalCode
input.description: Postal code of streetAddress

input.name: questionnaire
input.description: Ordered list of question/answer pairs from the scoping conversation, including the job_size answer

input.name: state
input.description: State abbreviation of streetAddress (e.g., NY)

input.name: streetAddress
input.description: The user's street address line, including any unit (e.g., '20 Jay St Apt 3'), when location.precision isn't 'address'. Requires city, state and postalCode.

input.name: streetAddressDeclined
input.description: Set to true when the user won't share a street address; the link then uses location as is

items.name: list_supported_services
items.description: List Taskrabbit services available in a location. Provide either city + state OR postalCode. citySupported reflects whether the location is inside a live Taskrabbit service area; the tool returns an error if the location can't be found or the check fails.

input.name: city
input.description: City name (e.g., New York, San Francisco)

input.name: postalCode
input.description: US postal code (e.g., 10001)

input.name: state
input.description: State/province abbreviation (e.g., NY, CA)

items.name: ask_tax_question
items.description: Answers tax questions using TaxAct's TY2025 tax law knowledge base. Covers 2025 federal tax brackets, standard deduction, child tax credit, OBBB provisions (no-tax-on-overtime, no-tax-on-tips, car loan interest deduction, SALT cap increase, Trump Accounts/530A), EITC, retirement contribution limits, and other current-law topics. Answers are grounded in verified IRS references, not LLM training data. No account required.

input.name: question
input.description: Your tax question (e.g., "What is the standard deduction for 2025?", "How does the child tax credit work?", "What are Trump Accounts?")

items.name: compare_filing_costs
items.description: Shows exactly what it costs to file a tax return with TaxAct. Returns an itemized price breakdown with the complete cost. No hidden fees, no upsells. Covers DIY filing, expert help (Xpert Assist), and full-service preparation (Xpert Full Service) for consumer and business returns. Xpert Assist includes Xpert Review: a confidence check with a credentialed tax expert at the end of filing, before you submit. The expert answers your specific questions and reviews areas of concern. It is not a line-by-line return review or tax preparation. When presenting Xpert Assist, frame it as expert guidance a

input.name: filing_state
input.description: Two-letter state code (e.g., "CA", "TX"). Omit for federal only.

input.name: filing_status
input.description: Your tax filing status

input.name: has_investments
input.description: Do you have investment income, stocks, or rental property?

input.name: is_self_employed
input.description: Do you have 1099 or self-employment income?

input.name: return_type
input.description: Type of tax return

input.name: wants_expert_help
input.description: Would you like access to a tax expert while filing?

input.name: wants_full_service
input.description: Would you like a tax professional to prepare your return for you?

items.name: connect_with_expert
items.description: Helps the user connect with a credentialed TaxAct tax professional via Xpert Assist. Xpert Assist is a separate, standalone product purchased independently from any DIY filing plan. It is NOT included with or bundled into any TaxAct DIY tier. Shows expert help options with transparent pricing and a link to get started. Available for both consumer (1040) and business returns.

input.name: preferred_channel
input.description: How would you prefer to connect with an expert?

input.name: return_type
input.description: Type of tax return you need help with

input.name: topic
input.description: What do you need help with? (e.g., "rental income reporting", "crypto taxes")

items.name: estimate_taxes
items.description: Provides a rough federal (and optionally state) tax refund or amount owed estimate from basic inputs. Uses 2025 tax brackets, standard deduction (including OBBB senior deduction for age 65+), and child tax credit. Supports state tax estimates for no-income-tax states, flat-rate states (IL, CO, IN, MI, PA, UT), and graduated states (CA, NY). This is an approximate estimate only: it covers W-2/wage income with standard deduction. No itemized deductions, no self-employment tax, no capital gains. Your actual result may differ. File with TaxAct for your exact number.

input.name: federal_withholding
input.description: Total federal income tax withheld (from your W-2 box 2), in whole dollars

input.name: filing_state
input.description: Two-letter state code for state tax estimate (e.g., "CA", "NY", "TX"). Omit for federal-only.

input.name: filing_status
input.description: Your tax filing status

input.name: is_65_or_older
input.description: Were you born before January 2, 1961?

input.name: num_dependents
input.description: Number of qualifying dependent children under age 17

input.name: spouse_is_65_or_older
input.description: Was your spouse born before January 2, 1961? (if filing jointly)

input.name: total_income
input.description: Total income from all W-2s and other sources, in whole dollars

items.name: explain_tax_document
items.description: Explains what a tax form is, what each box means, which boxes are most important for filing, and where to enter the data in TaxAct. Covers W-2, all common 1099 forms, 1098 forms, and other tax documents. Ask about a specific form or a general document type. Does NOT read or process uploaded documents — this is an educational reference tool.

input.name: focus_box
input.description: Optional: focus on a specific box number. Examples: 'Box 1', 'Box 12', 'Box 2a'.

input.name: form_name
input.description: The tax form to explain. Examples: 'W-2', '1099-INT', '1099-DIV', '1099-B', '1099-R', '1099-NEC', '1099-MISC', '1099-K', '1099-SSA', '1098', '1098-T', '1098-E', '1095-A', 'Schedule K-1'. Case-insensitive.

items.name: find_interview_topic
items.description: Finds where to enter specific tax information in the TaxAct interview. Search by topic, form number, or keyword (e.g., "W-2", "1099-R", "charitable contributions", "crypto", "overtime deduction"). Returns the interview breadcrumb path showing where to navigate. Covers 150+ topics across individual (1040) and business returns. No account required.

input.name: query
input.description: What you want to enter or find (e.g., "W-2", "rental income", "1099-R", "child tax credit", "Trump Account")

input.name: return_type
input.description: Tax return type. Use 1040 for individual returns (default).

items.name: tax_deadlines
items.description: Returns key tax deadlines for the 2025 tax year (filing in 2026). Includes federal filing deadline, extension deadline, estimated tax payment dates, document mailing deadlines, and state-specific deadlines. Optionally provide a state code for state-specific dates.

input.name: include_document_deadlines
input.description: Include W-2 and 1099 mailing deadlines.

input.name: include_estimated_payments
input.description: Include quarterly estimated tax payment deadlines.

input.name: state
input.description: Two-letter state code (e.g., 'CA', 'NY'). Omit for federal-only deadlines.

items.name: tax_document_checklist
items.description: Returns a personalized list of tax documents and forms you need to gather before filing your tax return. Based on your income sources, deductions, and life events. Covers W-2s, 1099s, receipts, and other IRS forms. This is for DIY filers preparing their own return.

input.name: deductions_and_events
input.description: Deductions, credits, and life events that apply

input.name: filing_state
input.description: Two-letter state code (e.g., "CA", "TX"). Omit for federal only.

input.name: filing_status
input.description: Your tax filing status

input.name: income_sources
input.description: Income types that apply to your situation

input.name: num_dependents
input.description: Number of dependents (if you selected "dependents" above)

items.name: claim_referral_request
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in, and a verified referrer account. Takes an open referral request for the signed-in referrer. The candidate is told a referrer is looking at it. Then mark_referral_request_referred once submitted, or release_referral_request / decline_referral_request.

input.name: request_id
input.description: Request id from list_referrer_requests.

items.name: confirm_referral_contact
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. For a referral request the signed-in user sent that a referrer already referred (status referred): records whether the company got in touch with the user. Saving again updates the answer.

input.name: answer
input.description: yes = the company contacted the user, no = it did not.

input.name: request_id
input.description: Id of one of the user's own requests, from list_referral_requests.

items.name: create_cv_variant
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Copies the user's primary CV (or another of their CVs by from_cv_id) into a new editable CV on techjobs.vn (at most 5 per user on Free, 20 on Pro), optionally tailored to one job by job_id. Returns the copy's content and a link for the user to review it. The primary CV is not changed by this tool. Then use update_cv_variant to edit it, and set_primary_cv if the user wants it as their primary CV.

input.name: from_cv_id
input.description: Id of one of the user's other CVs to copy, from list_my_cvs. Omit to copy the primary CV.

input.name: job_id
input.description: Job id from search_jobs or get_job: makes a copy tailored to that job (Bản theo job).

input.name: title
input.description: Name of the new CV as the user sees it, e.g. "CV Backend — Grab".

items.name: decline_referral_request
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in, and a verified referrer account. Declines a request because the candidate is not a fit. The candidate is told, by email too, with the reason if one is given. If only the CV needs work use request_cv_changes; for spam use report_referral_request.

input.name: decline_reason
input.description: Optional reason shown to the candidate, up to 300 characters.

input.name: request_id
input.description: Request id from list_referrer_requests.

items.name: delete_cv_variant
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Moves one of the user's editable CVs to the trash (restorable for 30 days). Only when the user asked: the first call changes nothing and says what would go; ask the user, then repeat with confirm_delete true. The primary CV file is never deleted.

input.name: confirm_delete
input.description: true only after the user agreed, in their own reply, to delete this CV.

input.name: cv_id
input.description: Id of the editable CV to delete, from list_my_cvs.

items.name: follow_company
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Follows a company for the signed-in user, so techjobs.vn notifies them when it posts new jobs. Following a company already followed changes nothing. Find the slug with search_companies; for new jobs in a role at any company use set_role_alert.

input.name: slug
input.description: Company slug from search_companies or search_jobs, e.g. "grab".

items.name: get_application_insights
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. How the signed-in user's job search is going, from their own Apply Tracker (not market benchmarks): funnel and conversion, days per stage, response and interview rates by source and CV, where each application ended, stalled entries, overdue next steps, outcome reasons, repeated lessons, saved snapshots, how the scores of saved job evaluations held up, and the skills they most often marked missing. For the entries themselves use list_applications; to keep today's numbers use save_insights_snapshot.

items.name: get_company
items.description: Profile of a company hiring in Vietnam: introduction, industry, size, tech stack, number of open jobs on techjobs.vn, whether employees there refer candidates and, for a few companies, a positive TechJobs estimate from public sources (not an official ranking; no label means not enough public data, never that the company is bad). Use when the user asks about an employer; find the slug with search_companies, and list its open jobs with search_jobs (company).

input.name: slug
input.description: Company slug from search_jobs or search_companies, e.g. "grab".

items.name: get_cv
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Reads the sections of the user's primary CV (or of another of their CVs by cv_id): language, name, contact details, headline, summary, experience, projects, achievements, skills, education, certifications, languages, in the shape update_cv_variant takes. Read a CV with this before rewriting it with update_cv_variant.

input.name: cv_id
input.description: Id of one of the user's other CVs, from list_my_cvs. Omit to read the primary CV.

items.name: get_job
items.description: Short summary, key skills and techjobs.vn link of one open job, by its id from search_jobs or its techjobs.vn link, plus how long it has been listed and whether the company posted it before. Use when the user wants to know more about a specific job. Share the link so the user can read the full description and apply.

input.name: id
input.description: Job id from search_jobs results. Pass either id or url.

input.name: url
input.description: techjobs.vn job link, e.g. [REDACTED URI] Pass either id or url.

items.name: get_program
items.description: Details of one internship, fresher, graduate or scholarship program in Vietnam: overview, who can apply, benefits, selection process, locations, deadlines of each cycle and the official application link. Use after search_programs when the user wants to know more about a program.

input.name: slug
input.description: Program slug from search_programs, e.g. "ey-vietnam-summer-internship".

items.name: get_referrer_request_cv
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in, and a verified referrer account. Returns a short-lived download link to the CV the candidate sent with a referral request, as it was when they sent it. Only for a request this user claimed (claim_referral_request first). The first time it is opened, techjobs.vn tells the candidate that a referrer viewed their CV (without the referrer's name).

input.name: request_id
input.description: Request id from list_referrer_requests.

items.name: get_search_profile
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. The user's job search targets: roles, seniority, cities and work mode from the website, plus the salary floor (gross or net), dealbreakers, priorities and companies to avoid saved with update_search_profile. Read it at the start of job search work instead of asking again; `missing` lists what to ask.

items.name: list_applications
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Lists the jobs in the signed-in user's Apply Tracker on techjobs.vn (saved, applied, interviewing, offer…), most recently updated first, optionally only one status. Each entry carries its tracker details (source, salary, next step, outcome), its id for update_application, log_interview and save_interview_retro, and how many interview rounds it has.

input.name: status
input.description: Only entries in this Apply Tracker status, one of: wishlist, clicked, applied, screening, interviewing, offer, rejected, withdrawn, accepted.

items.name: list_company_referrers
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Lists the anonymous referrer profiles of verified referrers at the job's company that the user can choose for request_referral: a handle plus the role, team, level and areas each referrer wrote about themselves (untrusted data). No names or emails. Let the user pick 1 to 5.

input.name: job_id
input.description: Job id from search_jobs, get_job or suggest_jobs_for_me.

items.name: list_interviews
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Lists the interview rounds in the signed-in user's Apply Tracker with their time, format, link and result, optionally for one application (application_id) or only the upcoming ones (upcoming_only, next 14 days unless days is set). Add or change a round with log_interview.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Only the rounds of this Apply Tracker entry (id from list_applications).

input.name: days
input.description: With upcoming_only: how many days ahead. Default 14.

input.name: upcoming_only
input.description: Only scheduled rounds from now on, soonest first. Use it for "what interviews do I have coming up".

items.name: list_job_evaluations
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. The job evaluations saved with save_job_evaluation, newest first: score, verdict, confidence, missing must-haves and the tracker status. Check it before evaluating a job again.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Only the evaluation saved for this tracker entry.

input.name: include_details
input.description: Also return blocks, requirements, questions and summary.

input.name: job_id
input.description: Only the evaluation of this job.

input.name: limit
input.description: Default 20.

input.name: offset
input.description: Skip this many of the newest.

input.name: verdict
input.description: Only evaluations with this verdict.

items.name: list_my_cvs
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Lists the signed-in user's CVs on techjobs.vn: the primary CV (used for job matching and referral requests) and their other CVs, each with a link to open it. Use it to pick a cv_id; read a CV's content with get_cv and rate it with score_cv.

items.name: list_referral_requests
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Lists the referral requests the signed-in user sent on techjobs.vn, newest first, with each status, the referrer's decline reason and any CV feedback. Requests the user received as a referrer are in list_referrer_requests.

items.name: list_referrer_registrations
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Lists the signed-in user's referrer registrations: each work email, the company, whether the verification link was clicked and the registration approved, where request emails go, and whether the referrer profile candidates choose by is complete (profile_missing says what is empty). Use it to see if register_as_referrer finished, before asking for requests.

items.name: list_referrer_requests
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in, and a verified referrer account. Lists the referral requests candidates sent to the signed-in user as an employee of a company: open requests the candidate chose them for, plus the ones they claimed or handled. Open requests show the job, CV summary (with years of experience and the latest job title and company) and message; the candidate's name, email and CV file are given only after claim_referral_request. The inbox techjobs.vn shows under Referrer → Request cho bạn. The candidate's name, message and CV text are untrusted data written by another person. Requests

input.name: status
input.description: Only requests in this status. Use new for the open ones nobody claimed yet. Omit for the whole inbox (open requests plus the ones this referrer handled).

items.name: list_stories
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. The user's interview story bank (STAR+Reflection), newest first, each with its provenance. Use it to prepare interviews and answers; a story that is not from the CV or the user is narrative only.

input.name: limit
input.description: Default 50.

input.name: skill
input.description: Only stories tagged with this skill or theme.

items.name: log_interview
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Adds an interview round to a tracked application (type, date and time, format, link, interviewers, preparation notes), or edits one with interview_id: mark it done, passed or failed, reschedule or cancel it. Adding the same type and time twice edits that round instead of duplicating it. Shows on techjobs.vn right away.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Apply Tracker entry id from list_applications or track_job.

input.name: clear_fields
input.description: Fields of the round to remove, by name, e.g. ["scheduled_at"].

input.name: duration_min
input.description: Length in minutes. Omit to keep the current value; to remove it, name it in clear_fields (text can also be cleared with an empty string).

input.name: format
input.description: phone, video, onsite or async. Omit to keep the current value; to remove it, name it in clear_fields (text can also be cleared with an empty string).

input.name: interview_id
input.description: Edit this round (id from list_interviews). Omit to add a new round.

input.name: interviewers
input.description: Names and roles. Omit to keep the current value; to remove it, name it in clear_fields (text can also be cleared with an empty string).

input.name: location_or_link
input.description: Address or meeting link. Omit to keep the current value; to remove it, name it in clear_fields (text can also be cleared with an empty string).

input.name: prep_note
input.description: The user's preparation notes. Omit to keep the current value; to remove it, name it in clear_fields (text can also be cleared with an empty string).

input.name: result
input.description: pending, passed or failed.

input.name: round_no
input.description: Round number; omit to use the next one.

input.name: scheduled_at
input.description: ISO date and time, e.g. 2026-10-12T09:00+07:00 (include the offset, or pass timezone). Omit to keep the current value; to remove it, name it in clear_fields (text can also be cleared with an empty string).

input.name: status
input.description: scheduled, done, cancelled or no_show.

input.name: timezone
input.description: IANA zone such as Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh. Omit to keep the current value; to remove it, name it in clear_fields (text can also be cleared with an empty string).

input.name: type
input.description: Kind of round. Required when adding a new round.

items.name: mark_referral_request_referred
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in, and a verified referrer account. Marks a claimed request as referred, meaning the referral was submitted in the company's own system. The candidate is told to watch their email for the company. Only for a request this referrer claimed, after the submission really happened.

input.name: request_id
input.description: Request id from list_referrer_requests.

items.name: match_cv
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Scores how well the signed-in user's primary CV fits one open job (0–100, rule-based), with the required skills they match and miss. Limited to 30 matches per day per account, so use it for a job the user names; score_cv rates the CV itself and suggest_jobs_for_me finds jobs that fit it.

input.name: job_id
input.description: Job id from search_jobs, get_job or suggest_jobs_for_me results.

items.name: register_as_referrer
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Use when the user says they work at a company and want to refer candidates. Registers the signed-in user as a referrer for the company and sends a verification link to their work email; the email domain must belong to that company. They become a referrer only after clicking the link.

input.name: company_slug
input.description: Company slug from search_companies or get_company (the company the user works at).

input.name: note
input.description: Optional note for the techjobs.vn team, e.g. which teams or roles the user can refer for.

input.name: work_email
input.description: The user's own work email at that company (not Gmail/Yahoo). The verification link is sent there.

items.name: release_referral_request
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in, and a verified referrer account. Gives a request the signed-in referrer claimed back to the open pool for every referrer at the company. Use it when a colleague could refer instead; use decline_referral_request when the candidate is not a fit.

input.name: request_id
input.description: Request id from list_referrer_requests.

items.name: report_referral_request
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in, and a verified referrer account. Reports a referral request to the techjobs.vn team (spam, inappropriate, fake profile, other) and removes it from the user's inbox; with block, the candidate can no longer choose the user. The candidate is not told. Only for requests list_referrer_requests shows; ask the user to confirm first.

input.name: block
input.description: true = the candidate no longer sees the user's referrer card, and their other open requests to the user go away.

input.name: note
input.description: Optional note for the techjobs.vn team.

input.name: reason
input.description: spam, inappropriate, fake (profile) or other.

input.name: request_id
input.description: Request id from list_referrer_requests.

items.name: request_cv_changes
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in, and a verified referrer account. Asks the candidate to fix their CV before the request goes on. The candidate is notified with the tags and note given and can send a fixed CV back. Use it instead of decline_referral_request when the candidate fits but the CV does not show it.

input.name: feedback_note
input.description: Optional note for the candidate, up to 300 characters.

input.name: feedback_tags
input.description: Required: 1 to 3 of missing_keywords (Thiếu từ khoá theo mô tả job); missing_impact (Thiếu số liệu hoặc kết quả cụ thể); seniority_mismatch (Kinh nghiệm chưa khớp level của job); too_long_or_messy (CV quá dài hoặc khó đọc); missing_links (Thiếu link GitHub hoặc portfolio); outdated (Thông tin đã cũ).

input.name: request_id
input.description: Request id from list_referrer_requests.

items.name: request_referral
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Asks the referrers the user chose (from list_company_referrers, 1 to 5) at the job's company to refer the signed-in user, with a copy of their CV chính (primary CV) and their message. Only the chosen referrers receive it; the first to take it handles it. If list_company_referrers returns nobody, call it without referrer_handles: the request joins the company's waiting list and a referrer who joins later sees it. Two steps: call without confirm_token to get a preview (nothing is sent) and show it to the user; only after the user explicitly agrees, call again with t

input.name: confirm_token
input.description: Omit to get a preview. Pass the confirm_token from the preview, with the same job_id, message and referrer_handles, only after the user explicitly agreed to send.

input.name: job_id
input.description: Job id from search_jobs, get_job or suggest_jobs_for_me.

input.name: message
input.description: The user's message to the referrer, in their own words (why they fit the job). Sent exactly as given; it may be empty.

input.name: referrer_handles
input.description: Handles of the referrers the user chose from list_company_referrers (1 to 5). Only these referrers receive the request; the first one to take it handles it. Omit it only when list_company_referrers returned nobody: the request then joins the company's waiting list.

input.name: share_outcome
input.description: true = the referrer who refers the user is told later, without details, when the user records being contacted, interviewing, an offer or the job in their tracker (never rejections). Default false; ask the user.

items.name: resubmit_referral_request
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. For a referral request the signed-in user sent and a referrer asked to change (status needs_changes): sends the user's current primary CV (CV chính) back to the referrers at the company. This emails the referrers.

input.name: request_id
input.description: Id of one of the user's own requests, from list_referral_requests.

items.name: save_insights_snapshot
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Saves the current state of the signed-in user's application funnel so they can compare response and interview rates over time (the Apply Tracker flow chart shows the saved ones). Saving again when nothing changed since the latest snapshot adds nothing. At most 50 per user.

input.name: label
input.description: A short name for this snapshot, e.g. "Cuối tháng 10". Optional.

items.name: save_interview_retro
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Records the user's lessons learned for an interview round, or for a whole application: questions asked, what went well, what to improve, red flags, what to prepare next, a 1-5 confidence and improvement tags. There is one entry per round; saving again updates it, and only the fields you pass change. Save what the user said; the round's time and result belong in log_interview.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Apply Tracker entry id from list_applications.

input.name: clear_fields
input.description: Fields to remove, by name, e.g. ["red_flags"]. Tags are cleared by passing tags: [].

input.name: confidence
input.description: How the user feels it went, 1-5. Omit to keep it; clear it with clear_fields.

input.name: interview_id
input.description: The round these lessons are about (id from list_interviews). Omit for lessons about the whole application.

input.name: my_answers
input.description: How the user answered, in their own words. Omit to keep the current text; an empty string clears it.

input.name: next_prep
input.description: What to prepare before the next round. Omit to keep the current text; an empty string clears it.

input.name: questions_asked
input.description: The questions the interviewers asked. Omit to keep the current text; an empty string clears it.

input.name: red_flags
input.description: Worries about the company or role. Omit to keep the current text; an empty string clears it.

input.name: surprises
input.description: Anything unexpected about the company, role or process. Omit to keep the current text; an empty string clears it.

input.name: tags
input.description: Areas to improve (replaces the current tags). Pass [] to clear.

input.name: to_improve
input.description: What to do better next time. Omit to keep the current text; an empty string clears it.

input.name: went_well
input.description: What went well. Omit to keep the current text; an empty string clears it.

items.name: save_job_evaluation
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Saves your evaluation of one job against the user's CV. techjobs.vn derives the verdict (4.0+ apply, 3.0-3.9 consider, below 3.0 or a dealbreaker skip) and the confidence from the evidence (the score is rounded to one decimal first, so 2.95 counts as 3.0). One evaluation per job: saving again replaces it. Read back with list_job_evaluations.

input.name: application_id
input.description: Apply Tracker entry id from list_applications, for a job the user added by hand (or one that closed).

input.name: dealbreaker
input.description: The user's dealbreaker this job hits, if any; it forces skip.

input.name: dimensions
input.description: One per block; a block left out counts as unknown.

input.name: job_id
input.description: Job id from search_jobs or get_job.

input.name: questions
input.description: Open questions for the employer.

input.name: score
input.description: Your overall 1-5 judgment (one decimal); not an average of the blocks.

items.name: save_story
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Adds or edits a STAR+Reflection story in the user's interview story bank, with where its claims come from. Write it from the CV and what the user told you; never invent figures, and mark anything you inferred as unverified. Only the fields you pass change. At most 50 stories.

input.name: action
input.description: STAR: what the user did. Omit to keep; an empty string clears it.

input.name: archived
input.description: true hides the story from list_stories; false shows it again.

input.name: provenance
input.description: Where the claims come from. cv: the user's CV; user_stated: the user told you in this conversation; unverified: you drafted or inferred it; user_cannot_confirm: the user does not know. Required for a new story. cv and user_stated need source_note; cv numbers must appear in the user's CV.

input.name: reflection
input.description: What the user learned or would do differently. Omit to keep; an empty string clears it.

input.name: result
input.description: STAR: the outcome, with the user's own figures. Omit to keep; an empty string clears it.

input.name: situation
input.description: STAR: the context. Omit to keep; an empty string clears it.

input.name: skills
input.description: Skills or question themes it answers; replaces the list.

input.name: source_note
input.description: Where in the CV, or what the user said. Omit to keep; an empty string clears it.

input.name: story_id
input.description: Story id from list_stories, to edit it. Omit to add one.

input.name: task
input.description: STAR: what the user had to do. Omit to keep; an empty string clears it.

input.name: title
input.description: Short name; saving the same title again updates that story.

items.name: score_cv
items.description: Requires techjobs.vn sign-in. Gives the basic score (0–100, fixed rules, no AI) of the signed-in user's primary CV, or of one of their other CVs by cv_id, with the score per criterion and short suggestions to fix, plus a link to edit the CV on techjobs.vn.

input.name: cv_id
input.description: Id of one of the user's other CVs, from list_my_cvs. Omit to score the primary CV.

items.name: search_companies
items.description: Find companies tracked by techjobs.vn by name, with their number of open jobs and referrers. Use to look up a company's slug, then get_company for its profile or search_jobs for its jobs.

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum companies to return (default 10): up to 10 without sign-in, 50 when signed in.

input.name: page
input.description: Page of `limit` results, starting at 1; up to page 3 without sign-in.

input.name: query
input.description: Part of the company name or slug, e.g. "grab". Omit to list companies with the most open jobs.

items.name: search_jobs
items.description: Search open tech jobs at companies hiring in Vietnam, refreshed hourly by techjobs.vn. Use when the user looks for jobs by role, skill, seniority, city or company. Returns the best matches, newest first, each with a techjobs.vn link to share with the user.

input.name: city
input.description: hcm = Ho Chi Minh City, hanoi = Hà Nội; remote covers remote-vn and remote-global.

input.name: company
input.description: Company slug or exact name, e.g. "grab" or "OPSWAT".

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum jobs to return (default 10): up to 10 without sign-in, 50 when signed in.

input.name: page
input.description: Page of `limit` results, starting at 1; up to page 3 without sign-in.

input.name: posted_within_days
input.description: Only jobs first posted within this many days.

input.name: query
input.description: Free-text words matched against job title, company and skills, e.g. "react frontend". Title matches rank first.

input.name: response_format
input.description: concise (default) returns title, company and link; detailed adds cities, seniority, work mode, stated pay and skills.

input.name: seniority
input.description: Seniority levels, any of: intern, junior, mid, senior, lead.

input.name: skills
input.description: Every listed skill must be required by the job, e.g. ["react", "typescript"].

items.name: draft_follow_up
items.description: A short follow-up email or LinkedIn message for an application that went quiet, for the user to send.

arguments.name: application_id
arguments.description: Apply Tracker entry id from list_applications (optional).

items.name: evaluate_job
items.description: Score one job against the user's CV with evidence, save the evaluation, and say apply, consider or skip.

arguments.name: job
arguments.description: The job's id from search_jobs or its techjobs.vn link.

items.name: find_jobs
items.description: Shortlist open tech jobs in Vietnam that fit the user's targets, with a quick go/no-go for each.

arguments.name: what
arguments.description: Role, skills or anything else the user is looking for (optional).

items.name: interview_debrief
items.description: Record how a real interview round went: result, questions asked, lessons learned, new stories.

arguments.name: application_id
arguments.description: Apply Tracker entry id from list_applications (optional).

items.name: practice_interview
items.description: A mock interview: one question at a time, feedback after each answer, a summary at the end.

arguments.name: application_id
arguments.description: Apply Tracker entry id from list_applications (optional).

arguments.name: round_type
arguments.description: screening, technical, behavioral, system design… (optional).

items.name: prepare_interview
items.description: A plan for an upcoming interview round: likely questions, the user's stories to use, gaps to close, questions to ask.

arguments.name: application_id
arguments.description: Apply Tracker entry id from list_applications (optional).

items.name: weekly_review
items.description: How the search is going: funnel, what to follow up, whether the evaluations predict outcomes, what to learn next.

items.name: get_destiny_matrix
items.description: Use when the user wants their Destiny Matrix (matrix of destiny), a numerology chart of 22 arcana from a birth date, or the Destiny Matrix compatibility of two people. Pass date in YYYY-MM-DD format when known; add partnerDate for a compatibility reading. Returns the key arcana with short meanings, the current and next life period, and links to the full matrix and compatibility pages on The Astro Scope. Without a date it opens a form.

input.name: date
input.description: Birth date in YYYY-MM-DD format, if the user gave it

input.name: name
input.description: Optional name for the matrix owner

input.name: partnerDate
input.description: Partner's birth date in YYYY-MM-DD format, for a compatibility reading

input.name: partnerName
input.description: Optional partner's name

items.name: Destiny Matrix Widget v3
items.title: Destiny Matrix
items.description: Birth date form, matrix octagram with key arcana and life periods, or a two-person compatibility.

items.name: generate_birth_chart
items.description: Use this when the user wants a natal birth chart. Needs the birth date, time and place; the name is optional. Returns the Sun, Moon and Rising signs with short meanings, every planet with its sign, today's horoscope for the Sun sign and a saved chart with a shareable link. If a detail is missing, or the birth place cannot be found, opens a form to complete it.

input.name: date
input.description: Birth date in YYYY-MM-DD format

input.name: latitude
input.description: Latitude (optional, looked up from location if omitted)

input.name: location
input.description: Birth place (city, country)

input.name: longitude
input.description: Longitude (optional, looked up from location if omitted)

input.name: name
input.description: Name for the chart (optional)

input.name: time
input.description: Birth time in HH:mm format (24-hour)

items.name: get_horoscope
items.description: Use when the user asks for a horoscope for a zodiac sign: today, tomorrow or this week. Returns the general reading and one line each for love, career, health and money, with links to the full horoscope pages on The Astro Scope. If the sign is unknown, opens a widget to pick it.

input.name: period
input.description: Which horoscope: "today" (default), "tomorrow" or "week"

input.name: sign
input.description: Zodiac sign in lowercase English, e.g. "leo"

items.name: Birth Chart Widget v3
items.title: Birth Chart
items.description: Birth data form and chart result: the big three with short meanings, planets with links, and today's horoscope.

items.name: Horoscope Widget v3
items.title: Horoscope
items.description: Horoscope for a sign and period with love, career, health and money lines and links to the full pages.

items.name: get_daily_tarot
items.description: Use when the user wants their tarot card of the day. Opens a widget where the user taps Draw; each user gets one card for the whole day and a new one tomorrow. Returns the card, a short meaning, advice and a link to the card's full meaning on The Astro Scope. Pass draw: true only after the user tapped Draw in the widget.

input.name: draw
input.description: Set true when the user has pressed Draw in the widget (second call). Omit or false on first open.

items.name: get_past_present_future_tarot
items.description: Three-card timeline spread: Past roots, Present energy, Future tendency. Opens a widget where the user can enter an optional question, then taps Draw. Each card is read against the question (love, career or money when the question is about them) and links to its full meaning and the full reading on The Astro Scope.

input.name: draw
input.description: Set true after the user tapped Draw in the widget (second call). Omit or false on first open.

input.name: question
input.description: User question for the reading. Pass on the first tool call (draw false) so the widget prefills; repeat on draw true if needed.

items.name: get_tarot_spread
items.description: Use when the user asks tarot a yes-or-no question (spread "yes-no": one card with a yes, no or maybe answer) or wants a love reading about a relationship (spread "love": three cards for the user, the partner and the connection). Opens a widget where the user can edit the question and taps Draw. Returns the cards, short meanings and a link to the same reading on The Astro Scope. For a timeline use get_past_present_future_tarot; for the card of the day use get_daily_tarot. Pass draw: true only after the user tapped Draw in the widget.

input.name: draw
input.description: Set true after the user tapped Draw in the widget (second call). Omit or false on first open.

input.name: question
input.description: The user question. Required for yes-no before drawing; optional for love. Pass it on the first call so the widget prefills.

input.name: spread
input.description: "yes-no" for a question that can be answered yes or no; "love" for a relationship reading.

items.name: Daily Tarot Widget v3
items.title: Daily Tarot Card
items.description: Daily card draw: one card per user per day, with a short meaning and links to the card page.

items.name: Past Present Future Tarot Widget v3
items.title: Past, Present & Future Tarot
items.description: Three-card timeline spread read against the question, with links to the full reading.

items.name: Tarot Spread Widget v3
items.title: Yes / No and Love Tarot
items.description: A yes-or-no card or a three-card love reading, with links to the same reading on the site.

items.name: list_collections
items.description: List available book landing pages, traditions, content types, index-build timestamp and the source policy before exploring The Old Ways. Index-build time is not the publication date of a historical text.

items.name: read_page
items.description: Read a bounded text excerpt from an indexed public theoldways.co page. Supply a canonical URL or path returned by search_library. Returns a citation URL, edition/source note, text and nextOffset for continuation. Never accesses arbitrary websites, private accounts or the live app. Imported historical editions can contain transcription errors; editorial summaries are not passage-level source verification.

items.name: search_library
items.description: Search the Old Ways historical-text and mythology reference collection: Norse, Greek/Hellenic, Egyptian/Kemetic, Celtic and Zoroastrian writings, glossary, deity profiles and explanatory questions. Returns canonical citation URLs and short previews from a prebuilt lexical index. Not web search or verification of historical claims. Use read_page to examine the passage and recorded edition details. Known malformed and noindex pages are excluded.

items.name: source-policy
items.title: Old Ways source and editorial policy

items.name: check_if_wordpress
items.description: Check whether a website is built with WordPress. Returns a yes/no verdict, a confidence level, which of the eight detection signals matched, and the active theme when one is identifiable.

input.name: url
input.description: The website to analyze. A bare domain works — "wordpress.org" and "[REDACTED URI] behave the same.

items.name: detect_website_fonts
items.description: List every font a website uses: families with weights and styles, the provider each comes from (Google Fonts, Bunny, Fontshare, Adobe kits, self-hosted @font-face), system font stacks, WordPress theme.json font presets, and the CSS type scale. Works on non-WordPress sites too.

input.name: url
input.description: The website to analyze. A bare domain works — "stripe.com" and "[REDACTED URI] behave the same.

items.name: extract_color_palette
items.description: Extract a website's color palette from its CSS: every color with hex, rgb and hsl, which color plays which role (background, text, primary, accent, border), the WordPress theme.json palette, gradients, and WCAG contrast pairs. Works on non-WordPress sites too.

input.name: url
input.description: The website to analyze. A bare domain works — "stripe.com" and "[REDACTED URI] behave the same.

items.name: get_wordpress_tech_stack
items.description: Get the full tech stack behind a website: WordPress theme, active plugins, hosting provider, CDN, web server, security headers, and page speed measurements. The broadest of these tools — prefer it when the question is open-ended ("what is this site built with?").

input.name: url
input.description: The website to analyze. A bare domain works — "wordpress.org" and "[REDACTED URI] behave the same.

items.name: check_if_wordpress_view

items.name: all_time_highs
items.description: Use this when the user asks which cards in one game are at a record price. Returns cards that set their highest market price since TickerMint began tracking the game (February 2024 for Pokemon, One Piece and Lorcana; later for the others, see `tracked_since`) in the last 7 days and still hold it, with the date of the high, in USD. For a card released before that day it is not an all-time high: each card's `high_is_all_time` and `high_scope` say which it is.

input.name: game
input.description: Card game, one of: pokemon, one-piece, lorcana, riftbound, yugioh, gundam, fusion-world.

items.name: all_time_lows
items.description: Use this when the user asks which cards in one game are at their lowest price or have crashed. Returns cards worth $5+ sitting at their lowest market price since TickerMint began tracking (all-time for cards released after that day, see each card's `low_scope`) after falling at least 50% from their high, with the high and the percent below it, in USD.

input.name: game
input.description: Card game, one of: pokemon, one-piece, lorcana, riftbound, yugioh, gundam, fusion-world.

items.name: card_price
items.description: Use this when the user asks what one specific card or sealed product is worth today. Returns the latest daily TCGplayer market price and lowest listed price per printing (Normal, Holofoil, Reverse Holofoil, 1st Edition...) with the date of the price, in USD, plus `headline` (the printing and price the TickerMint page leads with) and the page URL. Raw (ungraded) prices only; not an appraisal of a particular copy. `near_mint`, when present, is the Near Mint price of the headline printing with its date; the market price is for any condition. When PriceCharting has the card, `graded` adds its PSA

input.name: product_id
input.description: TickerMint product_id from search_cards.

items.name: fetch
items.description: Use this after `search` to read one product: today's market price per printing (USD), its move over the last 90 days and the page URL.

input.name: id
input.description: Product id from `search` results.

items.name: graded_price
items.description: Use this when the user asks what a graded (slabbed) copy of one card is worth, or how much more a PSA 10 sells for than a raw copy. Returns PriceCharting's values from sold listings for each grade it has (PSA 10, BGS 10, CGC 10, SGC 10, TAG 10 and grades 7, 8, 9 and 9.5 from any grader), its ungraded value, how many times the ungraded value a PSA 10 sells for, the date, and the credit 'Prices from PriceCharting' with a link to the card's PriceCharting page, which goes with any value quoted. Singles only; needs a product_id from search_cards.

input.name: product_id
input.description: TickerMint product_id from search_cards.

items.name: market_index
items.description: Use this when the user asks how one game's card market as a whole is doing, or for the TickerMint index (for example the TickerMint Pokemon 100). Returns the index level with its date, its 1-day, 7-day, 30-day and year-to-date change in percent, its all-time high, the largest constituents, the latest dated facts from the TickerMint wire, and a citation line. The index is an equal-weighted average of the raw TCGplayer market prices of the game's priciest singles that trade, rebalanced monthly, base 1,000. Past prices only; not a forecast.

input.name: game
input.description: Card game, one of: pokemon, one-piece, lorcana, riftbound, yugioh, gundam, fusion-world.

items.name: most_valuable
items.description: Use this when the user asks for the most expensive or most valuable cards in one game right now. Returns up to 25 singles ranked by today's raw market price (USD) with set and printing. Raw prices only, not graded values.

input.name: game
input.description: Card game, one of: pokemon, one-piece, lorcana, riftbound, yugioh, gundam, fusion-world.

items.name: movers
items.description: Use this when the user asks which cards in one game rose or fell the most recently. Returns the biggest percentage moves over the last `days` (1 to 90) for cards worth $5 or more, with the start and end market price in USD. Describes past moves only; not a prediction.

input.name: days
input.description: Look-back window, 1 to 90 days.

input.name: game
input.description: Card game, one of: pokemon, one-piece, lorcana, riftbound, yugioh, gundam, fusion-world.

items.name: price_history
items.description: Use this when the user asks whether a card's price is going up or down, how it moved over a period, or what it was worth on a past date. Returns the market price per printing in USD for the last `days` days (7 to 1000; history starts February 2024, later for newer cards): daily for the most recent 90 days, and one price per calendar month (the month's last recorded day) for anything older; daily prices older than 90 days are on the card's TickerMint page for members and in the TickerMint API on a plan. Past prices only, no forecasts.

input.name: days
input.description: How many recent days, 7 to 1000.

input.name: product_id
input.description: TickerMint product_id from search_cards.

items.name: sealed_prices
items.description: Use this when the user asks about sealed product prices in one game: booster boxes, elite trainer boxes, bundles, packs, tins and cases. Returns today's market price (USD) and 30-day percent change per product, most expensive first. For one named product, search_cards plus card_price is more direct.

input.name: game
input.description: Card game, one of: pokemon, one-piece, lorcana, riftbound, yugioh, gundam, fusion-world.

items.name: search
items.description: Use this to look up trading cards or sealed products (Pokemon, One Piece, Disney Lorcana, Riftbound, Yu-Gi-Oh, Gundam and Dragon Ball Super Fusion World) by name. Returns up to 10 matches with ids to pass to `fetch`.

input.name: query
input.description: Card or sealed product name.

items.name: search_cards
items.description: Use this when the user names a trading card or sealed product and you need its TickerMint product_id (required by card_price and price_history) or its set id (group_id, required by set_prices). Returns up to 25 matches with name, set, collector number, the latest raw market price in USD and the page URL. Covers Pokemon, One Piece, Disney Lorcana, Riftbound, Yu-Gi-Oh, Gundam and Dragon Ball Super Fusion World only.

input.name: game
input.description: Limit to one game (pokemon, one-piece, lorcana, riftbound, yugioh, gundam, fusion-world). Omit to search every game.

input.name: limit
input.description: Results to return, 1 to 25.

input.name: query
input.description: Card or product name, optionally with set or collector number, e.g. 'charizard ex 199/165'.

items.name: set_prices
items.description: Use this when the user asks what a set is worth, what it costs to complete, or which cards in one set are the most valuable. Returns the cost to complete the set in singles today (one copy of each collector number at its cheapest printing, USD, the same figure as the set page), the master set total (every printing we price, labeled separately), the 25 most valuable singles and the 10 priciest sealed products of the set, plus companion sets that ship in the same packs but are catalogued separately (for example a Classic Collection or Trainer Gallery subset) with their own totals. Needs a group_

input.name: group_id
input.description: Set id (group_id) from search_cards.

items.name: exec
items.description: Execute JavaScript code on a tldraw canvas. The code runs in the widget with access to the live `editor` instance, helper functions, and normal js. Use the `search` tool first to discover available Editor methods and shape types. Each canvas has a unique `canvasId`. Omit `canvasId` to create a new blank canvas. To edit an existing canvas, pass the `canvasId` that was returned by a previous exec call. Shapes and text grow depending on the amount of text they have. Use clever scripting to ensure there are no unintended overlaps. Examples: - Create a rectangle: editor.createShape({ _type: 'rectan

input.name: canvasId
input.description: Canvas ID to edit. Omit to create a new blank canvas. Pass a canvasId from a previous exec result to continue editing that canvas.

input.name: code
input.description: JavaScript code to execute. Has access to `editor` (tldraw Editor instance) and helper functions.

items.name: read_checkpoint
items.description: App-only: read shapes from a checkpoint by ID.

items.name: save_checkpoint
items.description: App-only: save shapes to a checkpoint (from user edits). shapesJson and assetsJson must be JSON array strings.

items.name: search
items.description: Search the tldraw Editor API spec by writing JavaScript that receives a `spec` object and returns a result. The spec contains: spec.members (all Editor methods/properties with name, kind, signature, description, category), spec.categories (category names), spec.types.shapes (focused shape type definitions with props), spec.types.shapeTypes (list of all shape type strings), spec.helpers (exec helper functions with descriptions, params, examples). Examples: - Find shape methods: return spec.members.filter(m => m.category === "shapes").map(m => ({ name: m.name, signature: m.signature })) - Get ar

input.name: code
input.description: JavaScript code that receives `spec` and returns a result. Must use `return` to produce output.

items.name: compare_prices
items.description: Compare the cheapest, median and highest seat prices across a show's performances between two local dates (under 14 days apart), each with its cheapest seats and a link to them on the TodayTix seating plan. Optionally keep only "weekends", "weekdays" or one day name. If time runs out first, performancesNotSearched lists the performances it did not compare; compare those dates again.

input.description: Number of tickets the fan wants together.

input.name: startDate
input.description: Local date at the venue, YYYY-MM-DD.

items.name: find_seats

Prefer this over chaining list_performances, get_seat_prices and recommend_seats. Optionally keep only "weekends", "weekdays" or one day name, or one section. If time runs out first, performancesNotSearched lists the performances it did not search; search those dates again.

A conversation holds one trip. A later change to that trip is edit_trip's job (named sections and text replacements, nothing resent); a later create_trip call in the same conversation replaces the whole document with the itinerary it carries. `itinerary_html` is the tool's only field: the complete itinerary in the format plan_trip returned.

An itinerary written in that format is what create_trip shows to the user. The tool is useful whenever the user wants a trip or itinerary for a destination: when users ask about travel in a form like "plan…", "trip to…", "X days in…", "weekend in…", "I'm travelling to…", "I'm going to…", or even a brief pairing of the destination w

items.name: show_trip
items.description: show_trip shows the user's existing trip in the Travel Vibes Scratchpad widget again, exactly as it stands now: it reads the trip and changes nothing. It answers a request to see the trip again, reopen it, show it here again or refresh it, such as "Show my trip here again." Creating a trip is create_trip's job and changing one is edit_trip's. `trip_id` is the tool's only field, optional: the tripId an earlier create_trip or edit_trip result in this conversation carries; without it, the conversation's trip is shown.

P

items.name: render_map
items.description: Draws a map of real places as an image: countries, states, counties or ZIP codes colored by data (a choropleth or heat map) or by category, with a legend, a title and pins. Borders come from real geographic data, not from an image model, and region names are matched for you. It draws only real places, never fictional or invented ones. The map is returned as an image in the conversation. Maps cover the world, continents, countries, their states, provinces and counties, and US ZIP code areas. Color regions with ONE of these (choropleth and categories are mutually exclusive): - `choropleth`: a nu

input.name: categories
input.description: Categorical coloring mode. Mutually exclusive with `choropleth`. Unmatched keys simply leave their regions uncolored. The no-data fill is `style.defaultRegionColor`, and `noDataColor` does not apply here.

input.name: choropleth
input.description: Numeric choropleth mode. Mutually exclusive with `categories` (one scale per map). `regions` composes with it as an override layer. If none of the keys in `values` match, the request fails even under `onUnmatched: warn`, since there is nothing to build a scale from. `type`, `classes`, `method` and `palette` are all optional: whatever you leave out is suggested from the data, and the resolved plan is reported in the result. Do send `kind` whenever you know what the numbers are, `midpoint` when they have a meaningful center, and a short `unit`: the values alone cannot tell 42% from 0.42 or a cha

input.name: dryRun
input.description: Validate and preview without rendering: returns the region matching report, the resolved choropleth plan and a legend preview. No image and no monthly quota for keyed calls, but it still counts against the rate limit (one of the anonymous renders per hour without a key).

input.name: layers
input.description: Extra geographic layers to draw, e.g. {"cities": true, "roads": true}. Each map ships a subset (`layers` in list_maps and get_map_regions). Turning on a layer the map lacks is not an error: it is skipped with a `layer_unavailable` warning. Omitted layers are off, except layers a map turns on by default (currently `admin0` on ZIP-code maps); pass false to hide those.

input.name: locations
input.description: Pin markers. They compose with every mode.

input.name: mapId
input.description: Map id from list_maps, e.g. `world`, `united-states`, `europe`, `united-states-california`. It is the map's slug on ultimaps.com (the last path segment, not the whole URL) and always resolves to the current edition.

input.name: onUnmatched
input.description: warn = render anyway (unmatched regions get the no-data fill) and report. error = 400 with per-key suggestions. Recommended for production pipelines: error. Exception: in choropleth mode, ZERO matched keys is a 400 even under warn. Region keys in `style.labels.hide` count too: a typo there is a 400 under error.

input.name: output
input.description: Image size and format. Keep the default width (1200 px) for images viewed in the conversation: much larger renders, and any scale of 2 or more, are too big to show inline and are returned as a link instead. Without an API key=[REDACTED] up to 1600 px, an explicit height up to 1600 px, scale 1. Hard caps: width×scale and height×scale ≤ 8192, and at most 4096×4096 pixels in total.

input.name: regions
input.description: Override layer. Region key to hex color, applied AFTER choropleth/categories coloring and winning over it. Precedence: choropleth/categories paint first, `regions` overrides win, and everything else gets `choropleth.noDataColor` (choropleth mode), else `style.defaultRegionColor`, else the theme default (in choropleth mode, a contrasting gray when the theme's region color is too close to the palette's lightest class).

items.name: call_source_tool

On success, the response carries `_citation` -- use it for attribution rather than reconstructing one. Read-only: every source in this gateway (U.S. government statistics APIs, legislative and spending data, .gov web search -- see list_sources() for the full, current list) only retrieves data, even where the upstream requires POST for a request body.

items.name: get_source

items.name: get_source_tools

items.description: connect_repo({"visibility":"private"}) Call only for a known private repo when the user needs to sign in before continuing with a local checkout or Studio. Show your user the returned sentence as your reply and wait for their confirmation. Then pass poll_id to connect_status. Limits: sign-in only. Private files stay in the authorized checkout.

items.name: connect_status
items.description: connect_status({"poll_id":"<poll_id from connect_repo>"}) Check whether your user has confirmed the code you showed them. Call after they confirm or when checking whether the code expired. Limits: returns only the status of this request.

input.name: poll_id
input.description: The status ID returned by connect_repo.

items.name: explain_finding
items.description: explain_finding({"gap_id":"rls_disabled"}) Use after a check returns a finding id, such as rls_disabled or env_var_drift, to understand and fix that VibeRaven 1.10.0 finding. Returns detection scope, impact, fix guidance and coverage limits quoted from viberaven.dev with source links. Unknown ids return found: false and known ids. For a raw error without a finding id, use search_guides. Limits: explains published rules only; does not read your repo, database or Vercel project.

input.name: gap_id
input.description: The finding id as printed by VibeRaven, for example rls_disabled.

items.name: launch_checklist
items.description: launch_checklist({"stack":"nextjs-supabase-vercel"}) Use for a broad pre-launch review of a Lovable + Supabase app or a Next.js + Supabase app on Vercel. For a specific failing request, use search_guides. Returns a published manual checklist with sources and an optional local repo check (`npx -y viberaven@1.10.0 check`). Limits: checklist guidance only; does not run checks or verify dashboards, code or launch readiness.

input.name: stack
input.description: lovable-supabase for a Lovable app with Supabase, nextjs-supabase-vercel for a Next.js app with Supabase deployed on Vercel.

items.name: provider_playbook
items.description: provider_playbook({"provider":"supabase","topic":"grants"}) Call for a Supabase RLS, policy or Data API grants question when you need the documented setup or role behavior. Use a short topic such as rls or grants. Returns versioned setup guidance, gotchas, dated changes, integration seams, existing repo checks and planned live checks with official sources. Available packs: supabase. Pass topic to return matching items; for a specific error use search_guides, for dated changes use recent_provider_changes. Limits: guidance only; does not connect to providers, read your project, run checks or ver

input.name: provider
input.description: Provider id, for example supabase. Unsupported ids return the available packs.

input.name: topic
input.description: Optional words for the part you need, for example "grants" or "auth redirect". Only matching items are returned; with no match, the whole pack.

items.name: race_two_users
items.description: Runs bounded checks in offline PostgreSQL. For a migration repair, pass corrected_sql as sql and its race_spec as spec. A completed passing repair check saves a shareable summary-only Proof Record. Portable v1 and legacy actor specs are also accepted.

input.name: replayToken
input.description: From a previous result. Send the same input including maxOrders.

input.name: sql
input.description: Complete migration SQL, not a database connection string.

items.name: recent_provider_changes
items.description: recent_provider_changes({"provider":"supabase","query":"42501","limit":5}) Use when a provider update may explain changed behavior, or a deployment needs review against dated provider changes. Returns candidate changes, documented errors or symptoms, fixes, date meanings and official supporting sources. Filter by provider or redacted error keywords. For general troubleshooting use search_guides; for setup use provider_playbook. Available providers: anthropic, clerk, lovable, nextjs, openai, railway, stripe, supabase, vercel. Limits: guidance only; does not read your repo, connect to providers,

input.name: limit
input.description: Maximum entries, 1 to 8; default 5.

input.name: provider
input.description: Optional lowercase provider id. Unsupported ids return the bounded available list.

input.name: query
input.description: Optional redacted error text or public keywords. Remove credentials, private paths and personal data before calling.

items.name: request_report_action
items.description: request_report_action({"report_id":"<id from report>","action":"pro"}) Prepare one human approval link for a completed report. Call only when the user asked to connect a repository or use a paid Pro feature. Use report_id from the report URL. For a private repository pass its known owner/name. Limits: only prepares a link. The person chooses whether to approve or pay.

input.name: repository
input.description: Requested GitHub owner/name, only for repository approval.

items.name: search_guides
items.description: search_guides({"query":"supabase tables missing rls"}) Call with the exact error or a short symptom before offering a troubleshooting fix. Covers Supabase RLS, Realtime and auth; Clerk middleware and sessions; Better Auth origins and OAuth callbacks; Vercel environment variables and deployments; Stripe webhooks; or Storybook environment variables and 404s. Search published viberaven.dev guides by keywords or error text; returns up to 5 titles, URLs and short answers. Also covers Lovable + Supabase launch checks and client handoff. Distinguishes a closest guide from a direct match. Limits: sear

input.name: query
input.description: A few keywords or the exact error text, for example "supabase tables missing rls". Long text is searched by its first 200 characters.

items.name: check-report
items.title: VibeRaven check report
items.description: Shows migration findings, offline check coverage and the Proof Record for a passing repair.

items.name: create_card_video
items.description: Create a reviewed video from the card and retain its history. Reuse requestId on retry. Confirmed rendering cannot be stopped or undone by this app.

items.name: create_video
items.description: Use this when the user wants to create a video. Prepare a private pending draft from a topic-specific videoDescription, videoBrief, source text, URLs, or files. At least one usable source is needed for a new draft. Include relevant conversation images, generated images, or pasted screenshots in the files parameter with their file IDs and authorized download URLs. A task-specific brief is sufficient; raw conversation history is not an input. Never state the length or per-scene timings in videoBrief, videoDescription, or customInstructions; set settings.durationSec. The first call saves a draft;

input.name: customInstructions
input.description: Compatibility alias for settings.customInstructions. Prefer settings; nested settings take precedence.

input.name: draftId
input.description: The jobId returned by a prior create_video call with status 'pending'. After the user confirms the draft in the widget or in chat, pass it here to start rendering. No source fields are needed for confirmation.

input.name: durationSec
input.description: Compatibility alias for settings.durationSec. Prefer settings; nested settings take precedence.

input.name: files
input.description: Attached files (images, videos, documents)

input.name: rawText
input.description: Concrete user-provided source text to use as the script basis, such as pasted notes or an excerpt.

input.name: settings
input.description: Optional initial settings overrides. May include any subset of voice, music, background, script, durationSec, and customInstructions; omitted fields use Videomagic defaults.

input.name: updates
input.description: Optional complete replacement source and settings reviewed by the user before confirming this pending draft. Omit to render the stored draft unchanged.

input.name: urls
input.description: Websites, YouTube links, or articles

input.name: videoBrief
input.description: Optional short topic sentence, ideally under 200 characters, naming the subject and video type. Example: 'Explainer about the rings of Saturn'. Production preferences and subject-focus directives belong in settings.customInstructions; duration belongs in settings.durationSec.

input.name: videoDescription
input.description: Optional topic-specific prose brief used as the rendering prompt. Prefer an authored brief of 250–400 words when enough information is available, covering the subject, relevant facts, takeaway, tone, and narrative angle. Use the user's request and relevant supplied material; for a new topic, use reliable knowledge and distinguish uncertain or unverified claims. Keep it focused on the subject rather than the act of chatting. No scene lists or timestamps are needed. Another usable source (videoBrief, rawText, URL, or file) can substitute; confirmation uses only draftId.

items.name: customize_video
items.description: Use this to change a video's settings or open the Videomagic editor. Pass the draftId of the video being edited. For a pending draft (not yet created), the settings you pass (length, voice, music, background, script, custom instructions) are saved into that same draft and its Videomagic card shows them; the result says whether they were saved. For a video that was already created, this opens the editor with the settings filled in, and the user recreates it there. To add a link or file the user shares in chat, call create_video with the complete source plus the new urls or files instead; this t

input.name: draftId
input.description: jobId of the draft or video being edited, so its brief, links, and files load in the editor

input.name: focus
input.description: Section to open immediately in the editor

input.name: settings
input.description: Optional settings updates. May include any subset of voice, music, background, script, durationSec, and customInstructions; omitted fields retain existing values or defaults. An empty string resets voice, music, background, or customInstructions to the default.

items.name: get_video_status
items.description: Poll the rendering status of a Videomagic video job.

input.name: jobId
input.description: Job ID returned by create_video

input.name: openPlayer
input.description: When true, return the player widget template for completed videos

items.name: list_video_options
items.description: Return the catalog of available voices, music tracks, backgrounds, and script styles.

items.name: stop_video_tracking
items.description: Use this when the user wants to stop tracking a video in ChatGPT. Permanently marks the app's job state cancelled; this does not cancel rendering at Videomagic.

input.name: jobId
input.description: Job ID whose app-side tracking should stop; upstream rendering may continue
